articles.title: Here’s what to expect at the opening of Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC trial
articles.summary:
THE HAGUE, Netherlands – On Monday, November 30, former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte is set to begin trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) over alleged crimes against humanity relating to his bloody drug war in the Philippines.

The much-anticipated trial phase is when the parties in the case, namely, the ICC prosecutor, the common legal representatives of the victims (CLRV), and Duterte’s defense team, will present evidence and witness testimonies. 

Unlike the confirmation of charges hearing last February, when the pre-trial chamber’s goal was to determine whether there was sufficient evidence in the prosecution’s case to proceed to trial, the judges in Trial Chamber III will now determine whether Duterte is guilty beyond reasonable doubt of the crimes against humanity of murder and attempted murder. 

The crimes were alleged to have been committed during Duterte’s anti-illegal drug operations as Davao City mayor and vice mayor, utilizing his so-called Davao Death Squad, as well as when he replicated the Davao model on a nationwide scale upon assuming the presidency in 2016.

Here’s what to expect when trial begins.

Plea entering

When trial opens, the judges will ask Duterte whether he understands the charges filed against him and ask him to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty.

The equivalent of this in the Philippine legal process is called an arraignment.

Opening statements

The ICC prosecutor and the victims’ representatives are expected to deliver opening statements after Duterte enters a plea. These are expected to take several hours each. 

The defense will deliver a short introduction of its case, but a longer opening statement is expected later in the trial.

Must Read

Duterte’s drug war was state-sanctioned, killed over 8,000 – Truth Commission

Witness testimonies

After the opening statements, the prosecution will begin presenting its witnesses. In the first weeks of the trial, that is, before the court goes on its winter recess on December 18, the prosecution is expected to present five witnesses.

The prosecution expects to present around 100 witnesses over the course of the trial.

“As with other complex cases involving allegations of crimes against humanity, these proceedings are expected to take some time. The exact duration of the trial will depend on a number of factors, including the volume of evidence, the number of witnesses, and any procedural matters that may arise during the trial,” said ICC spokesperson Oriane Huber Maillet in a briefing with reporters on Tuesday, November 24.

Only after the prosecution presents its case will the defense have the opportunity to present theirs. 

‘Fair trial’

The ICC presumes Duterte to be innocent unless and until proven guilty before the court.

“He is represented by counsel of his choosing and is entitled to all fair trial guarantees provided under the Rome Statute, including adequate time and facilities to prepare his defense, the ability to challenge the Prosecution’s evidence, and the opportunity to present evidence and witnesses on his own behalf,” said Maillet.

Victims’ participation

More than 500 victims of extrajudicial killings in Duterte’s drug war are authorized to participate in the trial through their team of legal representatives.

The ICC said it was taking steps to protect victims and witnesses from threats against their well-being.

How to follow the hearings

ICC hearings are public and can be followed in two ways: in person, by attending the hearings at the ICC’s headquarters in The Hague, or online via its Facebook and YouTube channels. 

Those who wish to attend the hearings in person may queue outside the court and are served on a first-come, first-served basis. There will be four sessions per day once trial begins, at the following schedule in local time at The Hague:

10:00 – 11:00 am

11:30 am to 12:30 pm

1:30 – 2:30 pm

3:00 – 4:00 pm

Viewers in the public gallery can watch the proceedings live, while online streams will have a 30-minute delay to allow for redactions in the event that confidential information is divulged during open session. The judges will occasionally call for a closed session to protect confidential information or participants.

“The Court remains committed to ensuring that these proceedings are conducted fairly, independently and transparently, in accordance with the Rome Statute and the Court’s legal framework,” said Maillet.

Demonstrations around the court

Both the pro- and anti-Duterte camps are expected to stage their own events and demonstrations in the days leading up to trial and when it begins.

On November 30, the Duterte Panagutin Network will hold a march and protest on ICC grounds, just before trial starts at 9 am. From 10 am onwards, Duterte’s supporters are expected to occupy the area in front of the ICC to stage their demonstration.

The ICC is set to begin Duterte’s trial amid a sharp delegitimization campaign from the former president’s supporters and global superpowers like the United States.

“The Court’s role is not to pursue any political objective. Rather, its role is to determine, through independent and impartial judicial proceedings, whether the charges have been proven according to the law,” said Maillet. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Liza Marcos in the House: Bojie Dy accompanies First Lady in Batasan visit
articles.summary:
Just an ordinary visit, or a possible courtship?

First Lady Liza Araneta made a surprise visit to the Batasang Pambansa on Tuesday, November 24, and of course, no less than Speaker Bojie Dy welcomed and accompanied her.

The joint public appearance comes amid rumors that Dy is being strongly considered to become President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s number two, should Vice President Sara Duterte be found guilty by the impeachment court and removed from office.

Malacañang or the House are unlikely to confirm anything more than what the visit was supposed to be on paper: the First Lady attending an arts workshop and storytelling session for children at the House.

Marcos, accompanied by Dy and other House leaders, checked the exhibits in celebration of National Children’s Month.

The Palace isn’t stupid and should be vetting by now all the possible replacements of Vice President Duterte, whose impeachment case is now in the final stages at the Senate.

Should at least 14 senators vote to convict her over her supposed unexplained wealth, the vice presidency will be a vacant position that the President needs to fill.

The Constitution allows the President to nominate a replacement from among members of the Senate and the House.

Aside from Dy, other lawmakers who are supposedly being considered for the job include Escudero, Win Gatchalian, Tito Sotto, and Lito Lapid.

As we previously reported, Dy is an attractive pick for the president. He does not have ambitions for higher office in 2028, sometimes plays second fiddle to the President’s son, Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, in the House, and is still respected by his colleagues despite the perceived ceremonial nature of his power.

Must Read

Bojie Dy, the unexciting Speaker whom Marcos can count on

While Sandro is a lawmaker himself, the President cannot pick his son because he is only 32 years old, below the constitutional age requirement of 40.

The First Lady is known to have the President’s ear, and insiders say she is actively involved in managing the many affairs of the Palace.

It wouldn’t be farfetched to imagine how the vice presidency problem could also be on her plate, but we can only speculate. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate passes 2027 OP budget in two minutes
articles.summary:
MANILA. Philippines – The Senate on Tuesday, November 24, swiftly approved the P10 billion proposed budget of the Office of the President (OP) for 2027 in just two minutes. 

Senator JV Ejercito, sponsor of the budget, noted during the plenary deliberations the new recommended appropriation for the OP is now P10.83 billion.

“Out of courtesy, and historically, we give due courtesy to the budgets of the Office of the President and Office of the Vice President,” Senate Majority Floor Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said in moving for the passage of the proposed budget.

Senate President Pro-Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III approved the motion sans objections. 

The OP initially sought P10.158 billion, roughly one-third of its current 2026 budget and over two-thirds of its 2025 budget, in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). 

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto previously said that the staggering budget cut was because the Philippines’ 2026 chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was lodged under the OP and is broken down based on the various agencies involved in the preparations related to hosting different meetings and the summits under the regional grouping. 

“We’re asking for less while remaining fully prepared to do more. We believe this amount is sufficient for the Presidency to meet the exacting demands of leading the nation at a time of overlapping domestic and external challenges,” Recto said during the OP’s budget briefing before the House committee on appropriations on September 1.  – Rappler.com

articles.title: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
articles.summary:
Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”.

The building, which was also attacked last Thursday, is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Houthis restarted in July.

Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The image showed some damage to the building about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact from a strike on the same tower on Nov 19, which caused damage but no injuries.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the image was taken or the extent of the further damage from the latest strike.

Saudi Civil Defence said the 11 people injured included two Saudi citizens, four Egyptian nationals, three Nepalese nationals and two Indian nationals.

“Relevant authorities responded to the incident immediately, implementing all established protocols and measures for handling such situations, and taking the necessary steps to ensure the safety of lives and property,” the Arabic statement said.

“One of the towers in the financial centre was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack,” coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post, without naming the building.

Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower is the most prominent landmark of King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD), a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s economic ambitions.

A witness told AFP that a vehicle fitted with a speaker had warned pedestrians in the area to take cover on Tuesday. No warning was sent to mobile phones about any threats to the capital.

Afterwards, police cars blocked some entrances to the gleaming financial district. With imposing skyscrapers, luxury shops and green spaces, the district also hosts the headquarters of the Saudi stock exchange along with multinationals such as Goldman Sachs.

An attack on the PIF is symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy — a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.

A tower belonging to state oil giant Aramco in KAFD was hit earlier this month, while Riyadh’s international airport was repeatedly struck in October, with one attack killing 14 people.

The Houthis, who control much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July in a knock-on from the US-Iran war.

The attacks have caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh, and forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer’s AFC Asian Cup.

Such cowardly attacks undermine peace efforts: Pakistan

Pakistan strongly condemned the “terrorist attack carried out today by the Houthi militia”, the Foreign Office said.

In a statement, FO said Islamabad denounced “such cowardly attacks, which endanger civilians and civilian infrastructure, heighten regional tensions and undermine efforts to restore peace and stability”.

“Pakistan stands in full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in the face of these attacks. The Kingdom has every right to defend its territory and protect its citizens and residents,” FO affirmed.

It expressed Pakistan’s deep sympathies with those injured and their families and wished them swift and full recovery. FO also commended the Saudi authorities for their “prompt response” and the steps taken to protect lives and property.

Islamabad has condemned Houthi attacks repeatedly, including on international platforms, and termed them a grave violation of the kingdom’s sovereignty.

Pakistan and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye.

Under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish leaders met in Riyadh in October and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said later that month.

‘26 killed in Yemen attack’

On the ground in Yemen, the war has caused a major humanitarian crisis, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced from their homes since July.

The Houthis have seized swathes of territory, forcing forces aligned with the internationally recognised government to stage a major retreat this month.

The Saudi-led military coalition has been striking Houthi targets in the impoverished country.

On Tuesday, local officials said a coalition airstrike on buses and trucks killed 26 people in Lahj province. On the other hand, government forces blamed the Houthis for the attack.

As the conflict shows no sign of slowing, Britain sanctioned the Houthis and four of its top officials “for deliberately attempting to undermine stability” on Tuesday.

The measures include an asset freeze against the group and an asset freeze and travel ban on four figures, including security and intelligence head Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani, and interior affairs official Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi.

The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognised government fleeing to Aden.

The war left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire went into effect in 2022.

articles.title: Huang’s return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
articles.summary:
Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as caution returned after Jensen Huang’s extraordinary return to AI giant Nvidia days after he was forced to resign, with investors bracing for further volatility in a key sector driving economic growth worldwide.

A day after Huang’s reinstatement as CEO drove Nvidia shares up more than 30 per cent, adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value, the euphoria dissipated as its stock lost almost 9pc mid-session.

Fellow tech behemoth and AI giant Anthropic also slumped, giving up around 12pc to $77.19, below its $83 price for last week’s IPO.

Monday aside, AI stocks had already sold off sharply throughout November on worries about profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector.

Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 2.3pc and the broader-based S&P 500 lost 1.1pc, while the Dow was just into the green around 1700 GMT (10pm PKT).

Europe’s main stock markets, which feature far fewer tech companies than their Asian and US rivals, finished a handful of percentage points lower after jumping on Monday in line with Wall Street.

Away from the tech sector, French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi revealed it would buy the US biopharma group Insmed, a specialist in respiratory treatments, for $41bn as it races to bulk up its development pipeline of new drugs.

Sanofi’s share price closed up almost 10pc following the news.

Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago over extramarital affairs, reportedly with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a senior Nvidia executive before US President Donald Trump noisily declared he should be brought back.

“Jensen’s return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade,” said Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at Saxo Markets.

“He is not just Nvidia’s CEO; he is arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem. His relationships with customers, suppliers and capital providers are difficult to replicate,” she said.

But “Jensen Huang alone cannot support the AI trade in the long term,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

“Nvidia’s stock price decline on Tuesday is to be expected after such a large rally in the previous session,” she added.

Analysts were in broad agreement that Huang’s return did not mean an end to probes or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for six months.

The company remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.

Monday’s Wall Street surge had propelled Asian markets earlier on Tuesday, with Taipei surging 9pc higher as chip titans TSMC and MediaTek added nearly 10pc each.

Seoul piled on more than 6pc thanks to strong gains in fellow chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung, and Tokyo rose nearly 4pc, led by a 12.5pc jump for semiconductor tester Advantest.

articles.title: Islamabad United snap up Matt Henry, Karachi Kings secure Adil Rashid as direct signings for PSL 12
articles.summary:
Islamabad United have signed New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry, while Karachi Kings have secured the services of England leg-spinner Adil Rashid as their marquee direct signings for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL).

Multan Sultans have also utilised the direct-signing facility, bringing Australian fast bowler Lance Morris on board ahead of the player auction scheduled for January 23, 2027.

Lahore Qalandars announced Sri Lankan batter Kamindu Mendis as their direct signing, while Quetta Gladiators have signed Lockie Ferguson.

Islamabad United unveiled Henry in an announcement on Tuesday, adding an experienced international campaigner to their bowling attack.

The 34-year-old New Zealand seamer has taken 199 Twenty20 wickets and is set to make his first appearance in the PSL after having featured in the Indian Premier League (IPL).

Karachi Kings, meanwhile, have opted for the experience of Rashid, a key member of England’s white-ball teams that won the 2019 ICC World Cup and the 2022 T20 World Cup.

The 38-year-old leg-spinner is renowned for his variations and ability to take wickets in the middle overs.

Although previously selected by Multan Sultans in a supplementary category, Rashid did not feature in the tournament after withdrawing due to international commitments. He will make his PSL debut with Karachi, with the deal reportedly valued at around Rs6.2 crore.

Multan Sultans have strengthened their pace department with the signing of Morris, nicknamed ‘The Wild Thing’ for his express pace.

The Australian right-arm fast bowler has limited international experience but has represented Melbourne Stars and Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash League. His ability to generate considerable pace is expected to bolster the Sultans’ bowling attack.

The direct-signing window, which opened on October 23 and closed on November 23, allowed each of the eight franchises to recruit one overseas marquee player who did not feature in either PSL 10 or PSL 11.

Under the regulations, a franchise making a direct signing will see its salary cap increase from Rs45 crore to Rs50.5 crore.

Each team can retain a maximum of seven players, including its direct signing, with the retention deadline set for January 13, 2027. Franchises retaining the full quota will be required to release one player from the highest price category of the previous auction into the general pool.

PSL 12 is scheduled to run from March 18 to May 2, 2027, with 44 matches planned across five to six venues.

articles.title: Govt reduces diesel price by Rs4 per litre, petrol by Re1 per litre
articles.summary:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of diesel by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs318 per litre and diesel at Rs353 per litre on Nov 25 (Wednesday).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: PTI moves IHC for live broadcast of Al-Qadir Trust case hearing
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has filed a petition in the Islamabad High Court (IHC), seeking live broadcast of the appeal proceedings in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case involving party founder Imran Khan.

Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, were convicted and sentenced in January 2025 in the corruption case. An accountability court found them guilty of receiving billions of rupees and hundreds of kanals of land from a real estate firm in exchange for legalising Rs50bn that had been identified and returned to Pakistan by the UK during the previous PTI government.

The petition was filed on Tuesday through Barristers Salman Safdar, Salman Akram Raja and other lawyers.

It argues that the case is a matter of national importance and that live broadcasting of Imran’s appeal proceedings is essential to ensure transparency, uphold justice and maintain public confidence in the judicial system.

Live coverage would allow the public to witness the proceedings firsthand and dispel speculation and misinformation, the petition states. It adds that justice must not only be done but must also be seen to be done.

The petition invokes Article 19-A of the Constitution, which guarantees citizens the right to access information on matters of public importance.

It also cites the live broadcast of the Zulfikar Ali Bhutto reference and proceedings in the Pervez Musharraf case before the Supreme Court. It notes that the IHC has previously issued directions for the live broadcast of proceedings in significant cases.

The petition also raises concerns about Imran’s alleged solitary confinement in prison, the denial of adequate medical facilities and restrictions on meetings with his family members and legal representatives.

It expresses concern over what it describes as prison authorities’ negligence regarding his medical condition, including blood pressure and treatment.

It further points out that details of the verdict and sentence in the Al-Qadir Trust case were reported in the media even before the formal announcement of the judgment, raising questions about the transparency of the judicial process.

The petition argues that live broadcasting would allow an independent assessment of all legal aspects of the case and requested the IHC to order the live broadcast of the complete proceedings of the appeal.

IHC has fixed November 25 for hearing appeals filed by Imran and Bushra against their convictions.

According to the cause list issued by the registrar’s office, a division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Mohammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif will take up the appeals.

The PTI founder and Bushra Bibi have challenged their convictions in the high-profile case and sought relief from the high court.

Last month, senior members of the PTI legal team approached the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), seeking early fixation of a criminal appeal filed by Bushra Bibi in the case.

The FCC rejected her plea seeking suspension of her seven-year sentence, observing that there were no sufficient grounds to interfere with an April 30 IHC order declining to suspend her sentence while her appeal remained pending.

Bushra, along with Imran, had initially moved the IHC for the suspension of her sentence in July last year. But the high court dismissed their requests in May 2026, observing that their appeals against their convictions had already been fixed for hearing.

articles.title: Rohail Nazir's fifty books Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-finals spot for Pakistan Shaheens
articles.summary:
An unbeaten half-century by Rohail Nazir, followed by a devastating bowling display, helped Pakistan Shaheens defeat Nepal by 96 runs in their final Group ‘B’ match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars at the University of Doha for Science and Technology on Tuesday.

The defending champions remained unbeaten in the tournament, winning all three of their group matches to qualify for the semi-finals, where they will face Bangladesh A on Nov 27.

Batting first, Pakistan Shaheens were in trouble at 66-6 in 16.5 overs before wicket-keeper-batter Rohail steadied the innings with an unbeaten 64 off 83 balls, hitting four fours and three sixes.

After Hasan Nawaz fell for 28 off 59 balls, leaving the Shaheens at 88-7, Rohail added 70 runs for the eighth wicket with Ahmed Daniyal, who scored 16 off 35 balls, to help his side reach 168 before being bowled out in 42 overs.

For Nepal, Rashid Khan claimed five wickets for 39 runs, while Abhishesh Gautam took two.

Nepal’s chase got off to a disastrous start as Muhammad Imran and Mohammad Hasnain reduced them to 15-4 inside six overs. Hasnain struck twice in successive deliveries to dismiss Ishan Pandey and Lokesh Bam without scoring.

Left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim then claimed three wickets as Nepal slumped to 59-9. Mayan Yadav offered some resistance with a top score of 41 off 50 balls but was trapped leg-before by Maaz Sadaqat as Nepal were dismissed for 72 in 17.3 overs.

Hasnain and Sufyan took three wickets each for 21 and 17 runs respectively, while Imran claimed two for 29.

Rohail was named player of the match for his match-winning innings.

articles.title: Fazl decries ‘state siege’, claims prevented from attending Lahore event
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Police began removing barriers around Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s place of stay in Lahore on Tuesday evening, with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief claiming he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

In a post at 10:40am, JUI-F said Fazl reached Lahore on Monday night and was scheduled to address lawyers today at a seminar at the invitation of the Lahore High Court Bar Association (LHCBA). However, due to police deployment, he was restricted from leaving his accommodation, JUI-F said.

JUI-F spokesperson Hafiz Ghazanfar Aziz said police began removing the hurdles by 7pm and informed Fazl that he was free to leave. However, the senior politician decided to stay in the city for the night.

Aziz condemned the alleged government action, calling it an attack on civil liberties and constitutional rights.

A city police officer, who spoke on condition of anonymity, also confirmed that police began “removing the barriers” by evening.

Meanwhile, a plea challenging the alleged “siege” of Fazl’s place of stay was filed in the Lahore High Court (LHC). On the other hand, the district administration also placed a three-day ban on public gatherings and “unlawful assemblies”.

In an earlier video message, the JUI-F chief alleged that he was under a “state siege” and that roadblocks and checkpoints across Lahore were preventing him from attending a multi-party seminar organised by the LHCBA.

Fazl thanked the bar association, its president and members for inviting him to address the seminar, but regretted that “state-imposed restrictions” had prevented him from attending in person.

He said the entire city had been “choked” by roadblocks and checkpoints, adding that peaceful citizens were being stopped from entering an environment of “intellectual discussion”.

“God willing, these sieges will break, these obstacles will be removed. Oppression never achieves permanence, but patience has always enjoyed permanence throughout history,” he said.

Fazl said his party had always worked for peace and had put its workers’ lives at risk for the country. He added that JUI-F did not need “a certificate of patriotism” from the rulers or any state institution.

“Neither from the rulers nor from any state institution have we come to obtain a certificate of loyalty to the homeland. In fact, I believe that perhaps we should be the ones issuing this certificate to people now. Their loyalties are questionable, whereas our loyalties are above all suspicion,” he said.

Claiming arrests of party workers and leaders in different areas, the JUI-F chief said his party would go ahead with its planned public conference in Sargodha on Nov 26.

He alleged that businesses were being shut down, shops and flour mills sealed, and party office-bearers arrested in Bhakkar, Mianwali, Khushab, Sargodha and its tehsils.

The JUI-F chief urged the public to make the gathering successful and demonstrate their commitment to freedom, constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and democracy.

“We are fighting the case of the public. We are fighting the case of Pakistan. We are fighting the case of this state,” he said.

Fazl alleged that the state had intensified its actions against JUI-F after the party exposed its role in matters concerning mineral resources in tribal areas.

He said his party was fighting for the rights of people across all provinces, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Sindh and Punjab, as well as Gwadar.

“These are the property of the people, not the property of the federation, nor the property of any single powerful institution, and we will not allow it to be looted by anyone,” he said.

Fazl said his party would remain steadfast in its position and take the matter to its “logical conclusion”. He reiterated his gratitude to the LHCBA and regretted that restrictions had prevented him from addressing its members directly.

Opposition leaders Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI MNA Asad Qaiser, and veteran lawyer Ali Ahmed Kurd were among the participants of the LHCBA gathering, videos showed.

Plea filed in LHC against alleged ‘siege’

The plea against the alleged “siege” of Fazl’s accommodation was filed before the LHC by JUI-F lawyer Advocate Abrar Hussain.

It has yet to be fixed.

In his petition, the lawyer alleged that around 3,000 police personnel had been deployed outside Fazl’s residence, effectively confining him to his house.

The petitioner said he had sought a copy of the legal order authorising the detention or confinement of Fazl by police officials, but authorities did not share any such document.

He further alleged that police had also denied him permission to meet the JUI-F chief.

The petitioner requested the court to direct the police to lift the “siege” of Fazl’s residence.

In a statement, the party’s spokesperson warned that arrests of JUI-F workers in different cities on Monday, followed by the alleged deployment of a heavy police contingent outside the party chief’s residence, would have political consequences for the government.

He said arrests, roadblocks, the sealing of businesses and the registration of FIRs could not deter the party from its struggle. The JUI-F, he added, would continue its efforts for the supremacy of the Constitution and the protection of people’s rights.

Section 144 imposed in Lahore

Separately, Section 144 was imposed in Lahore for three days, from Nov 24 to 26, according to an order issued by the deputy commissioner, a copy of which is available with Dawn.

The order cited reports from law enforcement and intelligence agencies about a “serious and imminent threat” to public peace, security and the safety of life and property across Punjab, including Lahore, from militant and terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.

It said assemblies, rallies, gatherings, sit-ins, processions, demonstrations and public meetings could become targets for terrorist attacks, adding that the possibility of an untoward incident could not be ruled out.

The order also expressed apprehension that certain elements could engage in activities likely to lead to unlawful gatherings, disturb public order and pose security risks, potentially resulting in the loss of life and property or damage to critical infrastructure.

Under the restrictions, a complete ban has been imposed on the assembly of five or more people, processions and gatherings in any public place, street, road, highway, motorway or open space. The order also prohibits inciting people to participate in unlawful assemblies.

However, the restrictions will not apply to marriage ceremonies, funeral prayers, burial gatherings, prayers in mosques and churches, official duties of government and semi-government organisations, and courts of law, the order stated.

Fazl-govt rift

Tuesday’s developments came amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October.

Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks against each other.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghouri had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz assures KP governor of continued support to eliminate terrorism
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of all possible cooperation on behalf of the federal government for the complete eradication of terrorism, durable peace and the welfare of the public in the province.

The premier made these remarks as he met with Kundi in Islamabad on Tuesday, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

During the meeting, he said that the sacrifices of the security forces and KP police in the war against terrorism in the province would not go in vain.

The federal government would continue to “fully support the implementation of the decisions taken at the apex committee meeting to completely eliminate terrorism”, he was quoted as saying.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing full support for the development of KP and the welfare of its people, saying that all possible resources would be mobilised to provide them with healthcare, education and other basic facilities, according to the PMO.

The premier directed that special attention be given to improving social development indicators in KP, including healthcare and education.

He said that attention would also be given to promoting sports facilities in the province and providing young people with opportunities for constructive activities, the PMO added.

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi briefed the prime minister on the ongoing efforts by himself and the KP Advisory Council to improve law and order in the province.

Separately, Kundi also met with President Asif Ali Zardari, a statement by the President’s Office said, where he briefed the president on the situation following Oct 11, particularly the security situation.

The meetings come weeks after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition.

On Oct 22, PM Shehbaz also chaired a meeting of the federal apex committee in Peshawar. He had vowed to take tough decisions, while reaffirming the Centre’s commitment to bringing peace to terrorism-hit districts in the province.

Last week, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir also reaffirmed the security forces “unwavering resolve” to decisively eliminate terrorism and preserve peace and stability of KP in close coordination with law enforcement agencies.

articles.title: Govt selects consortium of 3 foreign banks for $500m finance facility backed by MIGA
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday selected a consortium of three foreign banks to arrange a $500 million trade finance facility, backed by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), a member of the World Bank Group.

“Following a competitive selection process and receipt of bids from nine international financial institutions, the Finance Division, Government of Pakistan, has selected the following banks as financing partners for the facility,” the Ministry of Finance said in a statement.

The banks included Commerzbank, JP Morgan and Standard Chartered Bank. It added that this facility opened new avenues for international financing.

According to the ministry, the decision was taken in a virtual meeting held by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb with the senior leadership of a consortium of international banks and representatives of the agency.

The banks were selected on the basis of the most competitive financing terms offered to the government, it said.

“The one-year facility, renewable on a rolling 1+1+1 basis, will support the financing of essential imports and trade-related expenditures,” the statement said.

It noted that the transaction marked the government’s first-ever credit enhancement transaction with MIGA under its Trade Finance programme, while also representing the first-ever participation of Commerzbank and JP Morgan in commercial lending to the government.

“The strong response and participation from international financial institutions reflect growing confidence in Pakistan’s improving economic outlook and progress towards sustainable growth,” the ministry said, expressing the government’s appreciation for the interest shown by all participating institutions and its gratitude “for their time, effort and engagement throughout the process”.

It said the transaction marked an important step towards “mobilising private international capital through multilateral risk-mitigation instruments, diversifying external financing sources and exploring innovative financing structures, while maintaining prudent debt management and fiscal responsibility”.

The ministry said the government would work closely with MIGA and the selected banks to advance the transaction towards its timely execution, looking forward to building strong and lasting relationships.

articles.title: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
articles.summary:
A hundred members of the legal fraternity and civil society have called for the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments to be repealed, reacting to remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, whose party had made their enactment possible.

The 26th and 27th Amendments, enacted in October 2024 and November 2025 respectively, were passed by both houses of the Parliament amid outcry from the PTI-led opposition.

Last week, Bilawal — a strong advocate for both Amendments when they were passed — said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor mutual agreement; it was passed with brute majority”, and that the previous one did have mutual agreement.

He also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation.

Later, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution.

In an open letter on Tuesday, 100 individuals — mostly lawyers and also including activists and academics — called for both the 26th and 27th Amendments to be repealed.

“Pakistan’s constitutional order belongs to its people. It cannot be seized by a majority that its own members admit was never theirs to wield,” read the letter, also signed by retired Supreme Court Justice Mansoor Ali Shah.

The letter recalled that Bilawal “admitted that the 27th Amendment was passed neither through political consensus nor through agreement, but a ‘brute majority’”.

It demanded that the “constitutional order that existed prior to the 26th Amendment must be restored”, adding that any future reform of the judiciary must come through an “open and consultative process”.

The 26th Amendment carved a constitutional bench out of the SC, with its members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

A year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), which is said to have effectively dethroned the SC as the country’s highest judicial forum.

It also made significant changes to the judicial system and the military’s chain of command, and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges, including Shah, resigned in protest the day it became law.

Tuesday’s letter also called for reserved seats in the legislative houses to be returned to their “lawful claimants”, in an apparent reference to the opposition.

The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol.

Although an SC bench declared the PTI eligible for the seats, the order was not implemented and later overturned by the constitutional bench created via the 26th Amendment, which handed them to the coalition parties that challenged the 2024 ruling.

“The government cannot continue exercising parliamentary authority derived from a process that the governing coalition’s own leadership has now publicly called into question,” Tuesday’s letter read.

“These seats must be restored to their rightful claimants through the appropriate legal and constitutional mechanism,” it added.

The letter noted that Bilawal “described the way the opposition was stripped of its reserved seats as ‘a joke’ and said the treasury benches had simply put those seats ‘in their pockets’”.

“Most damning of all, he accused the ruling government of amending the Constitution using seats that are ‘not yours’,” the document added.

The signatories pointed out that these words came “from the government’s key coalition partner whose votes were required to pass both the 26th and 27th Amendments”.

It continued: “The treasury benches face a question they can no longer evade. Their own coalition partner says reserved seats were taken by parties that had no right to them.

“On what constitutional, legal or moral basis does the government then keep claiming the numbers through which the 26th and 27th Amendments were passed?”

The lawyers and activists noted that a two-thirds majority was the safeguard the Constitution demands so that “it cannot be changed without the genuine and lawful representation of the people’s will”.

However, a majority “made up with seats that were unjustly denied to the opposition is not the majority the Constitution demands”, they contended.

“An amendment passed on that basis holds no constitutional, legal, or democratic validity. An amendment passed without a legitimate two-thirds majority is void from its very inception,” the letter asserted.

It further said that these questions applied directly to the FCC, which “owes its existence wholly to the 27th Amendment”.

“Its jurisdiction, its composition and its authority all come from a constitutional change whose legitimacy is now openly repudiated by the very people who brought it into being.

“A court cannot rise higher than its source. An institution whose authors cannot defend how it was built has no foundation left to stand on,” the lawyer said.

“Pakistan has witnessed far too many admissions of wrongdoing that have led to no consequences,” the letter observed, noting that leaders acknowledge violations at press conferences, express reservations, and then “allow the very arrangements they condemn to continue unchanged”.

“This cycle must end. The question is no longer simply whether a wrong was committed, but whether consequences and meaningful action will follow.”

The signatories stressed this was a “moment to begin repairing the grave damage caused to the judiciary and the constitutional order”.

“Those in power have a choice. They can either continue to cling to an illegitimate majority or they can correct course.”

The signatories include former Sindh High Court Bar Association president Salahuddin Ahmed, ex-minister Shireen Mazari, ex-senator Afrasiab Khattak, ex-MNA Bushra Gohar, HRCP Chairperson Nasir Zaidi and economist Dr Kaiser Bengali.

The lawyers include Rida Hosain, Hassan Abdullah Niazi, Asad Rahim Khan, Abdul Moiz Jaferii, Khadija Siddiqi, Faisal Siddiqi, Abuzar Salman Khan Niazi and Zainab Shahid.

Rights activists, including Nighat Dad and Usama Khilji, and members of the Women’s Action Forum (WAF) were among other signatories.

articles.title: Punjab Assembly adopts resolution seeking tougher punishment for blasphemy
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday unanimously passed a resolution demanding legislation to make the punishment harsher under Section 298-A (use of derogatory remarks, etc, in respect of holy personages) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Currently, Section 298-A provides “imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years”, or fine, or both as punishment for “whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representation, or by any imputation, innuendo or insinuation, directly or indirectly, defiles the sacred name of any wife (Ummul Mumineen) or members of the family (Ahl-i-bait) of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him), or any of the righteous Caliphs (Khulafa-i-Rashideen) or companions (Sahaaba) of the Holy Prophet”.

The resolution, moved in the House by opposition MPA Rana Aurangzaib, contended that the existing penalty was “insufficient” for such an act which “hurts religious sentiments”.

The House urged the federal government to move on the matter on a “priority basis” and enact legislation needed to increase the penalty under Section 298-A.

It also called on the federal government to ensure effective lawmaking and implementation to uphold respect for religious sanctities and to maintain social peace and harmony.

In August 2023, Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill 2023 to increase the punishment under Section 298-A from three years of imprisonment to at least 10 years in jail.

However, then-president Arif Alvi returned the bill to Parliament.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan had noted that the bill would have made it “more difficult for the accused to obtain statutory bail, which will now be granted at the discretion of the court rather than as a legal right”.

It observed that “in general, blasphemy cases are often lodged by the police under pressure from far-right clerics or complainants with personal vendettas or to stem the risk of mob violence following mere allegations of blasphemy”.

articles.title: 'Carrying hopes of 250m people': Zeeshan Ali to be 'first' Pakistani astronaut in space aboard China’s Shenzhou-24
articles.summary:
Zeeshan Ali was named a crew member of China’s Shenzhou-24 space mission on Tuesday, which is scheduled to launch on November 25, with Ali set to become the first Pakistani to undertake an orbital space mission.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China, referred to Ali on X as “Pakistan’s first astronaut”.

Ali will also be the first foreign national to board Beijing’s Tiangong space station, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced.

“Pakistani astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali is the first foreign national to visit Tiangong,” CMSA Spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said during a press conference.

And the Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said the Pakistani astronaut was also the first international crew member to join China’s manned space programme.

CMSA’s Jingbo said that the Long March-2F rocket that will carry the crew into space will soon be filled with propellant. “The crew is in good condition and the space station is functioning normally, meeting all requirements for the mission,” said Jingbo.

According to the CMSA, the Pakistani astronaut will serve as a payload specialist during the mission and return aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked with the Tiangong space station in May.

China’s astronaut Tang Hongbo will command the mission, with Wu Yi serving as the mission pilot and Ali taking on the role of payload specialist, according to the CMSA.

The crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18am Beijing time (5:18am Pakistan time) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China.

In a video shared by the Chinese embassy in Pakistan, Ali said the “real challenge” was mastering the Chinese language, rather than centrifuge training.

Ali is expected to spend around a week in space, conducting various experiments alongside the Chinese crew. CMSA said that during the mission, the crew will conduct around 90 experiments.

The Chinese space agency said the mission’s objectives included conducting an orbital rotation with the crew of the earlier Shenzhou-23 mission, carrying out routine operations and maintenance of the Chinese space station, and continuing space science research, including experiments involving space payloads.

The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40.

Lai is Hong Kong’s first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard the space station.

After the new crew reaches the space station, Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.

Zhu will remain on board to complete China’s first full-year stay in space — a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.

Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Hongbo and Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space.

‘We have already made history’

Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan, Ali said he was “deeply grateful” to the Chinese government for helping “us realise our dream of going into space”.

He said he arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China a few months ago, carrying with him the hopes of 250 million Pakistani people.

Detailing his experience in China, he said what he gained had far exceeded his initial expectations.

“First, I have acquired space flight skills. The management, staff and instructors at the Astronaut Centre of China have provided me with comprehensive training […] Day after day, I take another step upward.”

Pakistani astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali. — Screengrab

He continued, “I have learned the Chinese language and developed a friendship with my Chinese colleagues. Now, I can communicate with my Chinese crewmates in Chinese.”

“We trained side by side, and our friendship embodies the friendship between China and Pakistan: higher than the mountains, deeper than the oceans, sweeter than honey and as vast as outer space.”

He said he had come to deeply appreciate the meaning of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s words: “Exploring the vast universe, developing the space industry and building China into a space power is our unremitting pursuit of the space dream.”

“Now, this dream belongs to me and also belongs to Pakistan,” he said, adding that it would become a reality through the Shenzhou-24 space mission.

Ali said he believed that “what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself”.

“This mission is not a finish line; it is a launch pad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, Mars and beyond.”

Ali noted that 2026 marked the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan space cooperation, as well as the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

“Together with my Chinese crewmates, I will show that this friendship is real — not only on paper, but also in orbit.”

Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali gesture as they attend a press conference before the Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission to China’s Tiangong space station, at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, near Jiuquan, Gansu province, China on November 24, 2026. —Reuters

Addressing Pakistanis, he said: “I now feel the true weight of the words of our Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, when he told me that we were about to write a new chapter in Pakistan’s history. I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulders, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis.

“To every child who is watching while I am in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams.”

In his message to his family, he said: “I want to say that I will travel farther from home than ever before. But I promise you one thing: whenever I look back at the Earth for the first time, I will always search for the light of our home before I look at anything else. No matter how far I fly, we will still share the same Moon, and I will still be looking back at the same Earth.”

He then thanked his teammates, those who supported him, his instructors, scientists, engineers, Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA.

“You are the reason that I am here today, and no matter who flies, we have already made history together,” he said.

Ali said the “two great nations of China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time. Now it is time to show this great achievement, innovation and send the world a message that we work hand in hand for the peaceful utilisation of space”.

Separately, China Daily posted a video of Ali saying that his planned one-year training had been compressed to seven months.

“That was the biggest challenge for me when I came here. But the real challenge, honestly speaking, was mastering the Chinese language. Learning the Chinese language is the key to the hearts of Chinese people,” he added.

Ali said he had read about several astronauts saying that whenever they looked at Earth from outer space, they did not see any borders or “separation between human beings; it is one humanity”.

He said he would be taking handwritten letters from his children and father on his journey “as a great source of inspiration”.

‘A moment that belongs to every Pakistani’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took to X to wish the crew his best for Wednesday’s liftoff.

“Tomorrow, Pakistan will look to the skies with anticipation, pride and deep gratitude,” he said, adding that as the Shenzhou-24 prepared to carry a Pakistani astronaut to Tiangong Space Station, the nation stood on the “threshold of a historic first”.

“It is a moment that belongs to every Pakistani,” he wrote and paid tribute to Suparco as well as academic institutions, scientists, the armed forces and national institutions whose efforts reflected “Pakistan’s growing capabilities and our determination to reach new frontiers in space exploration and scientific advancement”.

PM Shehbaz expressed gratitude to President Xi, stating that his “visionary” leadership had taken Pakistan-China friendship to an “unprecedented height”.

“This historic milestone is a powerful testament to the exceptional trust, mutual respect and enduring brotherhood that bind our two nations and peoples,” Shehbaz wrote, as he wished the crew his best for a safe and successful mission.

“Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas, in its journey to outer space.”

President Asif Ali Zardari also congratulated the nation on “historic” participation in the Chinese mission, calling it a “landmark achievement” and a “moment of immense national pride”, according to a statement issued by his office.

He said the mission reflected Pakistan’s “growing commitment to science, research and technological advancement”, lauding the role of Suparco, Pakistani scientists and China’s cooperation.

President Zardari expressed hope that the mission would open new horizons for Pakistan’s space programme and the scientific experiments undertaken during the mission would contribute to advancing research and knowledge.

“Pakistan’s participation in human spaceflight is not only about reaching space but also about harnessing its opportunities for research, learning and innovation.”

Citing a verse from national poet Allama Iqbal — Sitaron se aagay jahan aur bhi hain — he stressed that the mission should inspire Pakistan’s young generation to “pursue knowledge, innovation and scientific discovery with confidence and ambition”.

Planning Minister Iqbal said the joint mission marked “the trust and iron brotherhood between Pakistan and China”.

Sharing a photo of himself from the press briefing in Jiayuguan, Ahsan posted on X: “Filled with immense pride and excitement as I witness history in the making.

“Watching our astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, take centre stage is a deeply moving moment. We had dared to dream big and laid the foundational blocks for Pakistan’s space and science ambitions. Today, seeing those dreams take flight and come true right before our eyes reaffirms that no frontier is beyond our reach when a nation commits to knowledge, innovation, and perseverance. The sky is no longer our limit—it is our launching pad.”

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar congratulated the entire nation and Suparco as “Pakistan prepares to make history in space exploration and joint scientific advancement”.

“​This landmark moment speaks volumes about the strength of our all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. ​My sincere wishes go out to all the astronauts on board for a smooth and successful mission. Long live Pakistan-China friendship!” he posted on X.

“This achievement underscores the immense potential of Pakistan’s human talent and the enduring Pakistan-China friendship,” wrote the Foreign Office (FO).

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar highlighted on X that a Pakistani astronaut going into space was a source of joy and pride for the entire nation.

Earlier in April, astronauts Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were chosen from Pakistan to start training in China. Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

Eventually, Ali was chosen to join the Chinese mission.

Making the announcement, Iqbal wrote on X that he wanted to “honour both of our astronauts, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, selected for final training. They were chosen from among Pakistan’s finest pilots and scientists. They trained in centrifuges and simulators, in emergency drills and in a new language. Both performed exceptionally well in training. Though Zeeshan Ali will fly tomorrow, both have already made Pakistan proud”.

PM Shehbaz had met the two in April and congratulated them on their selection. He said the space mission was a “matter of pride for the entire nation” and further commended their “round-the-clock efforts” in achieving the milestone.

PM Shehbaz had hoped that the space mission would “add new dimensions to the brotherly relationship between Pakistan and China”.

Beijing has invested heavily in its space programme in recent years — catching up with its main rival the United States — and aims to land astronauts on the moon by 2030.

Pakistan is a natural partner, given the country’s decades-long, “all-weather” friendship. China is Pakistan’s largest trading partner and a major foreign investor.

China has been barred from participating in the International Space Station since 2011, when the US prohibited Nasa from collaborating with Chinese space agencies. Since then, Beijing has sought to build partnerships with other countries — including Pakistan — in its expanding space programme.

articles.title: Balochistan govt announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on wanted terrorists
articles.summary:
QUETTA: The Balochistan government has announced rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for providing authentic information about most-wanted terrorists in the province.

According to an official advertisement issued by the provincial government, a reward of Rs250m has been fixed for information about Bashir Zeb of the banned Balochistan Liberation Army and Abdul Rehman alias Rehman Gul.

Similar rewards have been fixed for other wanted persons depending on their status.

List of most-wanted terrorists and respective rewards on information regarding them issued by the provincial government. — via Saleem Shahid

The government said the list has been issued as part of its efforts to maintain law and order and eliminate terrorism in the province.

Balochistan Home Affairs Adviser Babar Yousafzai affirmed that the provincial government was determined to eradicate terrorism and protect the lives and properties of citizens.

The list of most-wanted terrorists and the announcement of rewards were, therefore, part of the ongoing government measures against terrorism.

Yousafzai stressed that public cooperation was of utmost importance in the war against terrorism.

The adviser appealed to the public to contact the relevant institutions of the government if they had any authentic information regarding the wanted terrorists.

He said the identity of informants would be kept anonymous, and immediate action would be taken against the terrorists. Payment of rewards would be made according to the rules and regulations fixed by the government.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, since the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks.

While Pakistan recorded fewer militant attacks from Nov 6 to 12, fatalities and injuries increased sharply, “highlighting the changing intensity and continued volatility of militant threat across the country”, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

Balochistan recorded 13 attacks, resulting in eight deaths and 19 injuries, while KP “remained the principal centre of violence” with 16 attacks and 44 fatalities.

articles.title: Hours-long road closures around Karachi’s PIDC junction cause traffic congestion
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Commuters in Karachi’s Saddar area faced traffic congestion on Tuesday after authorities closed some roads around the PIDC junction for a few hours in response to a sit-in call by the Sindh Indus Lawyers Forum (SILF).

In an alert issued at 1:16pm, Karachi Traffic Police said both roads from PIDC Chowk towards the State Life Building, as well as Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road, were closed to traffic.

In an update at around 6pm, the traffic police said the cut from PIDC Chowk towards State Life Building and both sides of Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road have been reopened to commuters.

As an alternative route, traffic was previously being diverted from PIDC Chowk towards Club Road and from the State Life Building towards Beaumont Road.

This screengrab from Google Maps shows traffic near the PIDC junction at around 4:30pm on Nov 24, 2026.

According to a statement issued by SILF, lawyers staged a sit-in outside the Sindh High Court.

They also staged a rally from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards CM House through Court Road, Sindh Secretariat Chowk, Sindh Assembly and Aiwan-i-Sadr Road.

The forum has put forward 16 demands under the banner of ‘Sindh Demands’, including opposition to the division of Sindh and the construction of Jalalpur Canal.

The protest call comes as a debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units, arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

The PML-N-led federal government has insisted on holding a referendum across the country on the establishment of new provinces or administrative units.

However, the suggestion has faced severe backlash from its ally PPP, with party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari saying that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

SILF said its demands also include “opposition to constitutional amendments and the proposed amendment”, apparently referring to the 26th and 27th Amendments, though no new amendment has been officially proposed.

Moreover, SILF’s demands, according to its statement, include stopping alleged irregularities in the Sindh Public Service Commission and alleged government intervention in lawyers’ bars.

“Corporate farming and mining in Karoonjhar mountain should be stopped and political prisoners should be released,” SILF further said.

On Sunday, a large number of people from across Sindh took to the streets of Karachi in a rally organised by the Jeay Sindh Rahbar Committee, an alliance of four nationalist parties, to protest against any plan for the creation of new provinces or administrative units in Sindh.

articles.title: Sales tax zones being established in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan, PM told
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed on Tuesday that separate sales tax zones were being established in the country’s four major taxpayer units — Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan — to improve collection.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the development was shared during a weekly review meeting concerning the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in Islamabad.

The move comes as the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection after 17 years, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection.

The statement released on Tuesday said that the meeting was also informed that work was underway to establish a modern cargo tracking system to address the sales tax gap and curb smuggling.

The system would digitally track the movement of goods from loading to delivery and comprise an electronic consignment note, a risk management system, field enforcement and an analytics dashboard, the statement said.

A steering committee with provincial representation was also being formed to oversee the system’s implementation, the PMO said.

The meeting was further informed that the FBR was establishing an office at Karachi’s Korangi Industrial Estate to provide services to local industrialists at their doorstep.

According to the PMO, PM Shehbaz directed authorities to expedite customs clearance, immigration and other operations at the country’s airports and make smart scanning systems operational at all international airports.

The meeting was informed that smart scanning systems were being installed at major international airports with the support of relevant agencies. The systems would automatically direct passengers’ baggage to the green or red channels.

The prime minister expressed the hope that the FBR chairman’s recent visits to Karachi and Lahore and meetings with local traders and industrialists would yield positive results for trade, exports and investment.

The meeting was informed that an audit of oil marketing companies’ bonded warehouses, conducted on the prime minister’s directives, had uncovered irregularities amounting to Rs24.4 billion. Recoveries were being made through legal procedures, the statement said.

It added that PM Shehbaz directed authorities to take action and make recoveries without discrimination.

The meeting was further informed that the Indus Collectorate had begun operations at bridges over the Indus River across the country. The enforcement collectorate, which had 856 staff members, had seized illegal goods worth Rs1.849bn in 302 operations so far, the statement said.

Regarding Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL), the meeting was informed that additional security features had been incorporated into several software systems to ensure data integrity. Departmental action was also being taken against FBR officers who had previously issued unauthorised consumption certificates under the FATA/PATA tax exemption, the statement said.

In 2009, the government transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise duty from Customs to the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) as part of a World Bank-backed reform aimed at integrating tax administration.

However, after 17 years of integration, the sales tax revenue gap has widened to an estimated Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax, raising questions about the effectiveness of the arrangement.

Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will handle sales tax and income tax separately, while both will continue to be administered within the IRS rather than through separate services.

articles.title: COP collapse
articles.summary:
THE collapse of climate negotiations at COP31 in Antalya recently is a stark reminder of a world disinclined to cooperate for the common good. The first climate conference to end without a deal since the 2009 Copenhagen Summit, COP31 succumbed to entrenched divisions among the delegates.

The main sticking point was the phasing out of fossil fuels, which was not mentioned in the draft agreement because of pressure from the petro-states including Saudi Arabia and Russia. This omission was rejected by the EU, Britain, and some small, climate-vulnerable states, which rightly hold fossil fuels responsible for global warming. Another stumbling block was the lack of commitment to providing climate finance.

Ironically, many of the countries that opposed the deal for not including the transition away from fossil fuels, refused to move forward on earlier pledges to provide and mobilise funding for poor climate-vulnerable countries. It has been noted, in fact, that many of the latter prefer funds over curbs on fossil fuels at this stage, given their need to rehabilitate lives already impacted by climate change and build infrastructure strong enough to withstand future shocks. This may have been one reason why some vulnerable countries curtailed their objections to the draft deal.

Day by day, the climate question is assuming greater urgency. Indeed, nature has been unrelenting against the backdrop of COP31. While Pakistan was largely spared the onrush of swelling rivers this year, Nepal witnessed a tragedy when a massive glacier collapse led to the flooding of vast tracts of land, killing hundreds. Heatwaves in Europe reportedly killed over 50,000 people last summer, while wildfires in Spain and France forced thousands of families from their homes.

“Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C raises the risk of irreversible changes […] along with devastating human impacts,” warns the UN’s main environmental agency in its latest Emissions Gap report. The need for cooperation and consensus on tackling climate change has never been greater.

Luckily, the failure of COP31 does not spell the end of climate diplomacy. International regimes built over years to combat a danger that knows no borders are too far advanced to come undone because an agreement was not reached in Antalya. But time is running out.

Given national interests and the nature of geopolitics, absolute consensus may be hard to forge. However, smaller regional initiatives, where countries — especially of the developing world — share green technology and other climate-friendly solutions can be pursued. These countries — which pollute the least but bear the brunt of global warming — have every right to ask for funds from the world’s chief polluters. The question is whether they have the will to safeguard their future through collective action.

Published in Dawn, November 24th, 2026

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official
articles.summary:
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year.

Israel’s military said it had struck a senior Hamas official.

Gaza’s interior ministry said an airstrike in Gaza City killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, director-general of the Internal Security Service.

Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the same strike in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood.

The strike comes as talks are underway in Israel to form a new government after October legislative elections produced no clear winner.

Centrist Gadi Eisenkot wants to form a coalition to end caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s long tenure.

But Netanyahu, who has staked his reputation on ensuring security for Israel after the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, remains in charge of military operations while negotiations continue.

Police station strike

Bassal said earlier on Tuesday that three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.

Three more were also killed in a third airstrike on a police station in the Al-Mawasi area in southern Gaza, he added.

Gaza’s police force said two policemen aged 23 and 33 were among the dead.

It condemned the strike as “part of an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus”.

Israel’s military said it “struck terrorists in the area” of the police station, but did not confirm the strike that killed the 17-year-old.

Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by the October 2023 attack.

More than 1,650 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the truce, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza health ministry.

In the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor. Most of Gaza’s population of 2.1 million live displaced in tents or makeshift shelters in the territory, where Israel’s military says it controls more than 60 per cent of the land.

articles.title: 'Watching me with eyes of fire': Pope Francis revealed in personal diary having seen devil
articles.summary:
The late Pope Francis recounted seeing the devil three times and, on one occasion, the “gate of hell”, in excerpts from his personal diary published on Tuesday in a new book.

The Private Diary of Pope Francis, by Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, includes passages taken from a journal the former Jorge Bergoglio kept between 1992 and 2024, a document that reveals his worries, regrets and self-critiques — as well as his enormous humanity and faith.

Fernandez, head of the Vatican’s Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, said he was asked by Francis to help make known to the world the musings inside the black plastic journal.
