Upon Francis’s death last year, Fernandez expressed concern to his successor, Leo XIV, that the book “might end up abandoned in a warehouse somewhere”. He was allowed to publish passages, noting that “the spiritual concerns present in his heart are very explicit and can be helpful to us”.

In one of the most intriguing revelations, Francis writes that while archbishop of Buenos Aires, he saw the devil three different times including “from the car when I was returning to the house, and in the choir loft during Mass” and once in Rome following a visit to Chile.

“I discovered that the devil had been brazenly lurking around cunningly,” wrote Francis in his journal on January 24, 2021, according to a copy of the English language version of the book published by Penguin Random House and viewed by AFP.

Francis wrote that he recalled three episodes “when I don’t doubt he was physically present”.

“More or less fifteen years ago. I saw him from the car window. I can’t forget his menacing and, at the same time, seductive eyes,” he wrote.

During the second episode inside a Carmelite chapel, Francis wrote: “He was watching me with eyes of fire”.

“I can’t forget that gaze, stronger than the previous. They were like flames of fire.”

The third episode occurred during a meeting in Rome, following a visit to Chile.

“I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything… I can’t forget the powerful raspiness of his voice,” he wrote, adding that “the Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and he thus freed me”.

Francis also revealed, on June 7, 2018, that on the night before, while getting ready to go to sleep, he “saw the entrance to hell”.

“Pagan seduction in full force. I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me,” he said, adding that he “grabbed the Rosary as a weapon”.

“It’s dangerous to approach the gate of hell because flames can leap out and burn,” he wrote.

Self critiques

Throughout the diary, Francis does not hesitate to criticise himself, for his occasional “feelings of disdain, envy, pride” or for having ignored a drunk man in the street who addressed him “because I wanted to have a serene walk”.

“The proud, self-sufficient, cynical, self-deceptive Jorge” is how the former pope described himself on December 30, 2022.

On January 15, 2017, he confessed that for a few days he had been experiencing “a very bad spirit of anger and discontent”.

While charismatic, Pope Francis also had a strong personality and was sometimes criticised within the Curia, the Catholic Church’s governing body, for being authoritarian.

Mercy is a recurrent theme in the journal.

“I felt, looking back, all the evil I’ve done in life. I’m in such abundant need of the Lord’s mercy!” he wrote on January 5, 1997.

End of life

Pope Francis appeared to worry that his days on Earth would be short-lived, fretting over his ageing and the need to “bear it”.

In 1996, at age 60 — nearly three decades before his death — he wrote: “I want to do good during the little time I have left, desiring to be good.

“How much time I’ve used badly! How much badly done!” In 2001, he wrote that “these 65 years make me think about the end. I’m already counting down”.

The worries continued even after becoming pope in 2013, with Francis writing on April 9, 2016 that “the attacks of the devil under different aspects have increased… Could it be a sign that my time is up and he doesn’t want to lose?” The journal contains 86 pages written before his election as pope in 2013, and another 55 written afterwards.

One of the briefest — and most moving — passages in Francis’s diary comes on July 21, 2013: “On March 13, they elected me pope.”

Francis died on April 21, 2025.

articles.title: Freedom of speech should not become a shield for those crossing 'red lines', says Naqvi
articles.summary:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Tuesday asserted that freedom of speech should not become a shield for those who cross “red lines”.

He made the remarks while addressing a seminar organised by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI).

At the outset of his speech, the minister said that there were four “red lines” for the state: terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence and sexual exploitation of children.

“On these four points, there is no compromise. Pakistan has paid for terrorism in blood. As interior minister, I have attended the funerals of martyrs. And very often, the hate that killed them began on a mobile phone,” he said.

He alleged that only 47 per cent of the complaints made by the Counter Terrorism Department were acted upon by social media platforms.

“This is not about technology, this is about people. We are not saying that free speech must be curtailed […] journalists must report, citizens must question, dissent must be heard, including against the government, but freedom of speech can never become a shield for those who cross these red lines,” he said.

He went on to say that Pakistan had “limited manpower”, resources and technology. Giving the example of Punjab, he said that the province had a population of 140 million against a strength of 61 people in the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).

“And these 61 people include drivers, clerks and officers. We cannot do this alone. That is why we have established a Social Media Protection Regulatory Authority,” he said.

The minister called for moving from policy towards enforcement.

“To begin with [social media] platforms, OTT services and major content creators must register with the authority. Registration is not a licence to silence anyone, it tells us who is accountable when something goes wrong,” he said.

He said that every social media platform “must name an empowered representative for Pakistan, who can actually take decisions”.

“Similarly, citizens need one complaint channel they can track. We are moving all NCCIA complaints onto the Pak ID app and the authority is building a single fully tracked complaint system,” he said.

Naqvi then went on to recount a recent town hall meeting, where he met five girls who were on the verge of ending their lives due to someone about to release “sensitive material” on social media platforms.

“We don’t have any pathway for approaching those platforms. It’s their responsibility to react immediately to save these innocent lives,” he said.

The minister said that the social media authority would verify whether action had been taken or not.

“Finally, enforcement will be step by step: engagement, then notice, then penalties. Blocking a whole [social media] platform will remain a last resort … our request will be clear, lawful and open to review,” he said.

“The state should not feel helpless. Yet, we see terrorist groups still recruiting, still raising terrorist funds, still spreading fear on these very platforms,” he said.

Giving an example, Naqvi said that the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) was a declared terrorist organisation, yet “many of their officials are still using these platforms”.

“If it is a declared [terrorist] organisation, then who allows them to move around and use all these platforms? Someone needs to stop [them]. This is our request,” he said.

“If you are not doing it, what meaning should we take? If it is declared by your country that this organisation is a blacklisted organisation, is a terrorist organisation and then you don’t take action, there’s a big question mark,” he said. He added that the government was focusing on the capacity building of the NCCIA.

“Today, I extend an open hand to all these platforms. Let us sit together, not across the table. Operate globally, be accountable globally and never let Pakistani citizens feel unheard,” he concluded.

articles.title: Eight killed, seven injured as passenger vehicle plunges into ravine in KP's Torghar
articles.summary:
At least eight people, including two women, were killed and seven others injured on Tuesday when a passenger vehicle plunged into a deep ravine in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Torghar district, Rescue 1122 said.

The accident occurred at Kundo Gigianay in Shatal Sira as the vehicle was travelling towards Jadba, according to the rescue service.

Rescue 1122 said the vehicle’s brakes reportedly failed, causing it to plunge into the ravine.

The injured included three men, three women and a child.

Rescue personnel shifted them to a basic health unit (BHU), where they received initial medical treatment, before transferring them to the District Headquarters Hospital in Battagram by ambulance for further treatment.

Three ambulances and 10 rescue personnel took part in the operation, Rescue 1122 said.

Earlier this month, three people were killed and 13 others injured when a coach collided with a motorcycle in Dera Ismail Khan.

The coach was carrying members of a Tablighi Jamaat group.

Earlier in the month, at least eight people were also killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a truck near the Havelian Interchange on Hazara Motorway.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates CDF Munir on Hall of Fame induction at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday congratulated Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on his induction into the Hall of Fame at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre.

“This distinction also reflects the enduring friendship between Pakistan and Malaysia,” the premier said on X.

“Field Marshal’s resolute leadership during Marka-i-Haq, unwavering commitment to national defence, invaluable contributions to promoting peace, and enhancing Pakistan’s standing internationally makes this honour truly befitting,” he added.

CDF Munir is on an official visit to Malaysia. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the visit aims to further strengthen bilateral defence and military cooperation between the two countries.

On Monday, ISPR said CDF Munir would also visit the National Defence Studies Centre, where a formal ceremony would be held to induct him as the 21st member of its “prestigious” Hall of Fame.

According to PM Shehbaz, the recognition belongs equally to the “brave” men and women of Pakistan’s armed forces, “whose courage, dedication and sacrifices safeguard our beloved homeland, and to the people of Pakistan, whose resilience and unwavering support remain our greatest strength”.

In a meeting with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim on Monday, CDF Munir reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties in Putrajaya. CDF Munir also held a meeting with Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled bin Nordin.

Last week, Malaysian High Commissioner Datuk Mohammad Azhar Mazlan reaffirmed his country’s commitment to strengthening its strategic partnership with Pakistan, highlighting longstanding political, economic, defence and cultural ties between the two countries.

He was addressing a gathering of Pakistani media representatives and members of the Malaysian community at the Malaysian High Commission.

In August, Pakistan and Malaysia agreed to establish a joint working group between their interior ministries to promote institutional cooperation, with a focus on counter-terrorism, counter-narcotics, cybercrime and the prevention of illegal immigration.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz takes notice of provocative statements by cabinet members, urges them to settle differences amicably
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Amid rising political tensions, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took notice of provocative statements by the federal cabinet members against each other and directed them to resolve their differences through consultation.

The remarks come amid a war of words between coalition partners over the past few days regarding a proposed referendum on the creation of new provinces, with a federal cabinet member publicly expressing his grievances against a colleague.

On Monday, PML-N Senator Rana Sanaullah said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had “complicated” the matter of creating new provinces by making an “irrelevant speech at an irrelevant forum”.

In his remarks, Sanaullah, who also holds the portfolio of inter-provi­ncial coordination, stood by his earlier criticism of the interior minister’s choice to start the debate on provinces while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad in July.

Naqvi had whipped up a political storm by calling for creating new administrative units in the country to “reset” the current “system” of governance. Following Sanaullah’s earlier remarks, Naqvi, without naming Sanaullah had warned last week, “The day I comment on this minister, he will not be able to show his face.”

In a statement issued by the PM Office on Tuesday, the prime minister took notice of recent statements by ministers and said the federal government’s entire focus was on public welfare projects.

“The government is continuing its journey from economic stability towards sustainable economic growth,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister said the federal government has always promoted the politics of development and progress.

“On this occasion, I direct all federal cabinet ministers to refrain from making political statements against one another,” the prime minister added.

“Matters among federal cabinet members should be resolved through mutual understanding and consensus,” the prime minister said.

He said statements by federal ministers against one another create a negative impression and divert attention from the politics of development and progress.

PM Shehbaz said federal cabinet ministers were performing well and should remain focused on public service, development and progress.

He said representatives of provincial governments should also refrain from making such statements and promote constructive dialogue.

“Statements against one another must cease completely. It is our collective responsibility to play an effective role in ensuring political stability,” the premier said.

Speaking to Geo News on Monday, Sanaullah had said it was his right as a colleague and as a political worker to express his opinion on Naqvi’s work.

The PM’s adviser contended that his colleague’s remarks at the business forum “complicated this issue, and today the matter… has become extremely controversial”.

“Now, if it comes to parliament, it will arrive in a controversial state,” he observed, affirming that his party will make all possible efforts to build a consensus.

The development came against the backdrop of a proposed referendum over the creation of new provinces. The issue gained renewed attention after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari opposed the creation of new provinces and the proposed referendum in a speech on Tuesday, warning that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry also insisted last week that a referendum on the matter “will happen”.

On November 12, Naqvi had floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

articles.title: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Indian skipper Shubman Gill’s call to overturn rule
articles.summary:
The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill’s call to allow the practice again.

Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India’s high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw.

However, AFP understands that the ICC has no immediate plans to relax the rule, which is treated in the same way as any other unfair method of changing the ball’s condition.

Saliva can materially alter the ball when mixed with sweets, chewing gum and mints and the practice is incredibly hard to monitor and regulate.

The ICC temporarily barred the practice of applying saliva as a precautionary measure during the pandemic in 2020 and two years later made it permanent.

The use of saliva to shine one side of the old ball and keep the other rough helps fast bowlers get the leather ball to swing late.

“I don’t understand why we haven’t been allowed to shine the ball yet – we are way past Covid times,” Gill said after the draw. “There was a rule that you can’t put saliva on the ball to make it shine. It’s been seven-eight years and I still don’t understand why they are not allowing it.

“I think this is also a big factor (in bowlers struggling to get wickets).” 

The tourists had declared their first innings on a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth day, but New Zealand survived 120 overs to finish on 239-5 at the close.

The Indian Premier League lifted its saliva ban last year, much to the bowlers’ delight, but the ICC finds no reason to relax it in international matches.

India and New Zealand now head to Christchurch for the second and deciding Test starting Friday, where both captains expect a more typical green, grassy and seamer-friendly wicket

articles.title: Imran wants PTI to expand political alliance, extend outreach to Fazl and other opposition parties, core committee told
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee has been informed that incarcerated party founder Imran Khan wanted it to expand its “political alliance” and extend outreach to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties.

Imran’s instructions were conveyed to the committee during an overnight meeting that began on Monday and during which lawyer Latif Khosa briefed the members on his meeting with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail earlier this month.

Khosa, along with another of Imran’s lawyers, Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet Imran and Bushra Bibi on Nov 11. The meeting, which was said to have lasted three hours, included discussions on Imran’s health, cases against him and the possible 28th constitutional amendment, the lawyers had said.

The PTI issued a statement after Khosa briefed the party’s core committee on the meeting.

“The core committee was informed that Imran Khan had expressed his complete confidence in the opposition leadership. He directed that the political alliance be further expanded and that outreach be extended to Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties, with the objective of forming a broader political alliance and initiating vigorous political activities,” the statement said.

Early in November, leaders of opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen-i-Pakistan, which includes the PTI, had met Fazl and the two sides had agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination.

Opposition parties appear to have increased coordination after the Oct 11 imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — where the PTI had been in power — which also drew criticism from Fazl.

Meanwhile, tensions between the JUI-F chief and the federal government have escalated since mid-October, with Fazl accusing the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the ruling PML-N in the Centre and the PTI.

New provinces

Khosa also briefed the PTI core committee meeting, which was chaired by party chairperson Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, on Imran’s instruction regarding the debate on creating new provinces.

The committee was informed that Imran had instructed that the matter concerning the creation of new provinces be “deliberated upon in detail at the forthcoming meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party”.

The recommendations formulated following those deliberations would subsequently be presented to Imran for his decision, the statement said.

Imran’s health

The committee was also briefed on Imran’s health and “expressed serious concern over their medical condition” and demanded the immediate implementation of the Supreme Court’s decision of Aug 18, in which the authorities had been directed to transfer Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private health facility in Islamabad.

The committee also demanded the immediate implementation of judicial orders concerning Bushra Bibi’s medical treatment.

Earlier this month, the Islamabad High Court had directed proper medical care and hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi, in line with prison rules.

The statement also referred to a recent letter written by Imran to top judges, saying that the core committee expressed “deep concern over the apprehensions raised by Imran Khan regarding his health and medical treatment”.

Reiterating its previous demands, the committee “urged the honourable judges to take immediate and serious notice of the matters raised in Imran Khan’s letter and ensure the prompt implementation of judicial orders concerning his medical treatment”, the statement said.

The committee also called on “the chief justice to […] ensure unrestricted access of Imran Khan’s personal physicians to him and facilitate his comprehensive medical examination and appropriate treatment”.

“Imran Khan must also be granted access to his family members and legal representatives. The committee emphasised that his health requires urgent judicial attention and that any further delay is unacceptable,” the statement said.

Detentions

Moreover, the committee “strongly condemned the continued detention” of Sohail Afridi — who has been rendered non-functional as the KP chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule — and other PTI lawmakers.

“The committee particularly condemned the extension of detention orders under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) against elected representatives and political workers” and maintained that the “continued detention of elected representatives and political workers, and restrictions on their political activities, are contrary to fundamental constitutional, democratic and human rights”, the statement said.

The core committee appealed to the Federal Constitutional Court and its chief justice to “suitably modify the existing stay order concerning Section 3 of the MPO and provide relief to political leaders and workers who had been granted bail by the Peshawar High Court before Nov 5 but whose release orders remain unimplemented owing to the stay order”.

The committee demanded the immediate removal of legal impediments preventing their release, the statement said.

The committee also decided to observe Nov 26 as the “Martyrs’ Day” to commemorate the loss of lives during the 2024 protests.

In the protests in Islamabad on Nov 26, 2024, deaths were reported among both the protesters and the security personnel.

articles.title: Tech firms soar as Huang’s return reinvigorates AI trade
articles.summary:
Technology firms rocketed Tuesday as Asia joined a global stock surge following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia boss less than two weeks after stepping down over extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy.

The Silicon Valley giant’s resignation on November 12 sent shockwaves through markets and dealt a severe blow to the AI trade, which was already under pressure amid worries over profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector.

His role as a fixer and visionary in an industry that has fuelled a tech revolution and a global economic boom was seen as crucial to the firm’s future as well as the AI buildout.

News of his return — announced soon after the opening bell Monday — lit a fire under equities, sending shares in Nvidia soaring an eye-watering 31.5 per cent and adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value.

Other Wall Street titans also enjoyed much-needed buying, pulling the Nasdaq up more than 6pc, the S&P 500 4.7pc higher and the Dow 3pc higher.

And Asia, which had started the week on the back foot, followed suit.

Taipei was the standout, blasting more than 9pc higher as chip titans TSMC and MediaTek added 10pc each, and Seoul piled on more than 6pc thanks to gains of around 8pc in market heavyweights SK hynix and Samsung.

Tokyo was lifted four percent by spikes of 14pc in Advantest, 11 percent in Tokyo Electron and 8pc in Kioxia.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Manila also joined in the fun with healthy advances.

“Jensen’s return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade,” said Saxo Markets’ Charu Chanana.

“He is not just Nvidia’s CEO; he is arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem. His relationships with customers, suppliers and capital providers are difficult to replicate.

“(His) return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia’s leadership crisis.”

And National Australia Bank’s Gavin Friend said: “The AI trade has been given a reprieve, with Huang’s reinstatement assuaging fears of any unravelling of the circular financing activity that has been a key support for the sector.”

However, analysts added that Huang’s reinstatement — which President Donald Trump said followed his own direct contacts with the company’s board — did not mean an end to probes or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for the past six months.

The company is still under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill.

Huang reportedly had a relationship with Alice Huang — who is not related — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. The group is under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.

Just this weekend, The New York Times added further details to the allegations, saying Alice Huang had been in touch with China’s top spy agency during the secret affair.

The United States on Monday added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips.

Oil prices continued to fall after Monday’s sharp drop that saw WTI back below $80 for the first time since August.

The latest selling was fuelled by hopes for an end to the Iran conflict as Axios reported US Vice President JD Vance met the prime minister of Qatar, which has acted as a mediator in efforts to resolve the near nine-month conflict.

articles.title: Collision between bus, truck kills 11 in UAE
articles.summary:
Eleven people were killed when a bus and a truck collided in Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), authorities in the Gulf nation said on Tuesday.

“Investigations into the circumstances and causes of the accident are ongoing,” the Ministry of Interior stated on its X account.

According to the ministry, emergency teams were dispatched to the accident site immediately after receiving the report. They launched rescue and emergency response operations in coordination with ambulance services, Civil Defence and other relevant authorities.

The response also included securing the scene and managing traffic, it added.

The ministry said the findings of the investigation would be announced once it had been completed.

It also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, praying for mercy and forgiveness for the victims and patience and strength for their loved ones.

The ministry urged the public to exercise caution, rely on official sources for information and refrain from circulating rumours or unverified reports about the accident.

It is the second major road accident to occur in the UAE this month.

On November 12, a multi-vehicle pile-up in Fujairah killed 14 people and left 30 others injured after a truck driver lost control of his vehicle and struck several other vehicles.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
articles.summary:
Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, though the government said she can only return through extradition.

It is the first time Hasina, 79, has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and where violence has risen since she sought a new passport and other documents earlier this month.

In addition to seeking the paperwork, cancelled months after she fled to Delhi following the uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement.

“Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th.” The government, however, reiterated that she can only be extradited by India, having been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising. Hasina has denied the charges from exile.

“She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance,” Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh’s minister of state for foreign affairs, told Reuters.

India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s extradition request and wanted to “engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties”.

On the request to arrange a flight, Kobir said: “Bangladesh will not entertain any such delusional request”.

Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was unreasonable for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.

A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on return and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power.

articles.title: 2027: NUC considers four-week break to mobilise university dons for polls
articles.summary:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The National Universities Commission (NUC) has said it is considering a three-to-four-week break in university academic activities to enable lecturers and other university personnel to participate in the 2027 general elections.

The Commission also pledged to mobilise Vice-Chancellors across the country to nominate credible and non-partisan academics to serve as Collation and Returning Officers during the elections.

The Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, stated this in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, led a delegation of National Commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the Commission.

Ribadu said the NUC would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of suitable academics, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process.

He also promised to issue a circular to universities upon receiving a formal request from INEC.

On the proposed academic break, Ribadu said the Commission would consult Vice-Chancellors to determine how best to adjust academic calendars without disrupting the electoral timetable or adversely affecting students’ academic activities.

“We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he said.

Emphasising the importance of credible electoral personnel, the NUC boss insisted that academics and other ad hoc officials deployed for election duties must demonstrate neutrality and integrity. “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” he stated.

Ribadu said that, beyond providing personnel, the NUC might propose a broader collaboration between the two institutions that might include internship opportunities for university students at INEC offices, the possible introduction of programmes in electoral studies and joint research in artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics.

He also suggested that university students could support voter education through campus clubs and other platforms, particularly in tackling misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections.

Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute. He expressed confidence that INEC would deliver transparent, free and fair elections capable of serving as a model for other African countries.

Earlier, the INEC Chairman, Amupitan, described the visit as a strategic engagement aimed at strengthening the partnership between the two institutions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He acknowledged the significant contributions of Nigerian universities to the electoral process over the years, particularly the deployment of Vice-Chancellors and other academics as Collation and Returning Officers.

Amupitan disclosed that INEC was introducing technological, operational and security reforms to improve election management and guarantee the safety of academics serving as electoral officials.

He said polling unit results recorded on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

The INEC chairman also announced the procurement of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines, a development expected to reduce the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine.

As part of its preparations, he said the commission would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

On security, Amupitan disclosed that the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to Local Government Areas and Registration Areas, with dedicated security cordons and escort arrangements around collation centres.

He further cited provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalising violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, noting that INEC had powers to prosecute offenders. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” he assured.

Amupitan also requested the NUC’s support in four key areas, namely the timely nomination of qualified and non-partisan academics, adjustment of university calendars, collaboration on campus voter education and countering disinformation, as well as improved welfare and recognition for academics deployed for election duties.

The Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6, 2027.

 

The post 2027: NUC considers four-week break to mobilise university dons for polls appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Reps move to refocus social investment programme
articles.summary:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

The House of Representatives has passed through second reading a bill seeking to amend the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, to reposition and refocus the agency for better performance, improved efficiency and more effective delivery of social investment programmes across the country.

The proposed legislation, which is sponsored by the Deputy Speaker, Benjamin Kalu, and six others, seeks to strengthen the institutional framework for the coordination, implementation and monitoring of social protection interventions in the country.

Essentially, the proposed legislation seeks the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as additional components of the Agency, as well as the establishment of the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central coordinating and data-management office for national social safety-net programmes.

Kalu, in his lead debate, stated that the strength of a social investment programme should not be measured by the size of its budget or the number of programmes it carries, but by whether the vulnerable citizens it was designed to reach can actually feel its impact.

He explained that the proposed amendments recognise that effective social investment requires more than individual programmes operating independently, noting that it demands an integrated system in which beneficiary data is properly managed, programmes are coordinated, and state and local governments are effectively engaged.

According to him, “The strength of a social investment programme is ultimately measured not by the size of its budget, nor by the number of programmes it carries, but by whether the vulnerable citizen it was designed to reach can actually feel its impact. Social investment is, at its core, a promise of the Nigerian State to stand between vulnerability and destitution, and to ensure that temporary hardship does not become permanent exclusion.

“The National Social Investment Programme Agency was established to give institutional structure to that promise. However, as the scale and complexity of our social protection landscape continue to evolve, there is a compelling need to strengthen the architecture through which these programmes are coordinated, implemented and monitored.

“This Bill therefore seeks to reposition and refocus the Agency for better performance and improved efficiency, while establishing clearer institutional responsibilities and stronger coordination mechanisms.”

articles.title: Alleged cyberbullying: DSS asks court to foreclose Sowore’s defence for exceeding adjournments’ ceiling
articles.summary:
The Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to make an order foreclosing the defence of African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore,, in his ongoing trial for alleged cyberbullying.

Counsel to the DSS, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, informed Justice Mohammed Umar shortly before adjournment, that an application has been filed to the effect.

Kehinde told the court that Sowore’s legal team had already been served with the application.

The senior lawyer, who submitted that Sowore exceeded the five adjournments he is entitled to in criminal trial by nine, said there must be an end to this.

“Before we finally draw the curtain to the proceedings, I want to bring to your lordship notice the application we filed and and served on the defendant.

“The application is that, there must be an end to all these. The defendant has since exceeded the number of adjournments as required by law,” he said.

He urged the court to allow the application to be taken.

In the motion on notice filed on November 23 by Kehinde, the DSS sought two orders.

The security agency sought an order of the court ordering the closure of the case for the defence.

It also sought an order directing the parties to file and exchange their final written addresses within such time as the court shall direct, and fix a date for the adoption of the said addresses.

Giving a nine-ground argument, the lawyer said Sowore was in the suit and was re-arraigned on a two-count charge on which he pleaded not guilty on Jan. 19, 2026, and thereafter the trial commenced.

He said the DSS called its witness and closed its case in March 2026, and the defendant’s no-case submission was overruled on 8th May, 2026 and he was called upon to enter his defence.

The lawyer said Sowore, as particularised in the affidavit in support of the motion, sought or procured an adjournment of the proceedings on at least 14 occasions.

He said eight of the adjournments were sought since he was called upon to enter his defence.

“This is far in excess of the five (5) adjournments to which a party is entitled under Section 396(4) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015.

“Since the defendant/respondent opened his defence on 6th July 2026, the trial has not progressed beyond the evidence of two defence witnesses,” he said.

Kehinde said Sowore has repeatedly filed applications and processes which had the effect of stalling the trial, including the subpoena issued against him, the lead counsel to the complainant/applicant).

He said the court has on several occasions warned Sowore against further delay.

According to him, the right to fair hearing guaranteed by Section 36 of the Constitution is a right to an opportunity to be heard, not a right to an unlimited number of adjournments.

He argued that a defendant who has been afforded ample opportunity to present his defence and fails to use it cannot complain of a breach of that right.

‘Section 36(4) of the Constitution guarantees a fair hearing within a reasonable time, and the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015 requires that criminal trials proceed from day to day or, where that is impracticable, within the strict limits on adjournments prescribed by Section 396 of the ACJA.”

Kehinde urged the court to grant the application in the interest of justice.

Responding, Reuben Adakole, who appeared for Sowore, acknowledged the receipt of the application seeking to foreclose their defence.

Adakole, however, said that before the prosecution’s application could be taken, the court needs to deliver its ruling on the objection raised by Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman, against their subpoena, including their preliminary objection and ex-parte motion.

“In as much as the application tends to foreclose us, there is our application which the court ought to pronounce on first. Until after the ruling, we can look at it. The application is unripe my lord,” he said.

Kehinde, however, corrected Adakole’s impression that the prosecution’s request was to get a date to hear the application seeking the foreclosure of Sowore’s case.l

The post Alleged cyberbullying: DSS asks court to foreclose Sowore’s defence for exceeding adjournments’ ceiling appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Olowolafe: Quality teachers key to Nigeria’s economic growth
articles.summary:
Dr Tunji Olowolafe, Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU), has described teachers as critical drivers of Nigeria’s economic development, while commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Minister of Education for advancing the Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme.

Olowolafe made this submission while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State, on Monday, November 23, 2026.

Speaking on the theme, “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the reform as a landmark development that would restore the dignity of Colleges of Education, strengthen teacher preparation and expand opportunities for prospective educators.

He applauded President Tinubu for signing the Federal Colleges of Education Act in 2023 and the Federal Ministry of Education for operationalising the programme in May 2025. Under the five-year arrangement, students can obtain an NCE after three years and proceed to earn a Bachelor’s degree within the same institution after another two years.

According to him, the reform combines practical teaching skills with academic depth, making graduates better equipped to teach across basic and post-basic education levels, particularly at a time Nigeria faces an estimated shortage of one million teachers.

He also highlighted the contributions of TETFund and NELFUND to educational development, citing SACOETEC as a practical example of the impact of sustained intervention. He observed that approximately 80 per cent of the College’s buildings were funded through TETFund, while encouraging eligible students to take advantage of NELFUND’s financial support for tuition and upkeep.

A major thrust of the lecture was the relationship between quality teaching and economic prosperity. Olowolafe described what he called a virtuous circle in which excellent teachers produce knowledgeable, skilled and innovative citizens, who drive business productivity and economic growth, ultimately expanding the resources available for further investment in education.

He maintained that teachers are much more than classroom instructors, describing them as nation-builders who shape minds and character at the most formative stages of life. He stressed that Nigeria cannot aspire to greatness without investing in the quality, capacity and welfare of its teachers.

He consequently advocated curriculum reforms that prioritise vocational education, practical skills, technology and problem-solving, while urging educators to embrace artificial intelligence without losing the human qualities of empathy, patience and moral guidance that define effective teaching.

Demonstrating the importance of recognising excellence, the Chancellor announced annual incentives through the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation for outstanding students and lecturers at the College. The initiative will reward the best NCE and degree graduates, first-class degree holders, NCE distinction graduates and lecturers rated highest by students, as an encouragement for hard work and higher academic standards.

He also announced plans by the Foundation to establish a solar-powered GOMTECH ICT centre at SACOETEC, equipped with Starlink connectivity to promote digital learning, artificial intelligence and technology-driven education. The Foundation will fund, equip and co-manage the facility in partnership with the College.

Olowolafe urged the graduating students to see their qualifications as a foundation for lifelong learning and leadership, citing former Nigerian leaders and nation-builders, including Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Shehu Shagari and Chief Obafemi Awolowo, who all had teaching backgrounds.

He challenged the graduands to appreciate the responsibility of their chosen profession, insisting that the quality of teachers Nigeria produces today will significantly determine the quality of its future leaders, workforce and overall national development.

The convocation lecture was attended by members of the College’s Governing Council and Management, academics, students, graduands and other stakeholders in the education sector.

The post Olowolafe: Quality teachers key to Nigeria’s economic growth appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Billboard controversy: Senator Orji Kalu’s politics anchored in the people, not Billboards — Reality organisation
articles.summary:
Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, clarifying that the billboard was neither erected nor commissioned by the former Abia governor.

The organisation, in a statement signed by Dimgba Okereke on Tuesday, disclosed that the billboard was erected by Engr. Emeka, a prominent son of Arochukwu, who independently chose to identify with the three political leaders.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu neither erected nor commissioned the billboard. It was the independent initiative of Engr. Emeka, a well-known son of Arochukwu, who chose to express his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti.

“That is his personal choice and democratic right. His preference should not be misconstrued as evidence of a political alliance between the individuals or their respective political parties,” the organisation stated.

Reality Organisation noted that Kalu’s political engagements over the decades had been anchored in grassroots relationships and direct interaction with the electorate rather than publicity materials.

“Senator Orji Uzor Kalu’s politics is anchored in the people, not billboards. For decades, he has maintained direct relationships with communities and ordinary citizens. His ongoing community-to-community engagements across Abia North are consistent with his longstanding approach to politics and representation.

“The OUK Movement and Reality Organisation have established grassroots structures built over several years through direct engagement with communities and voluntary participation by members and supporters.

“Senator Kalu cannot be held responsible for every independent expression of support by those who admire him. Neither can he be expected to stop individuals from expressing their political preferences within the confines of the law.”

The organisation stressed that democracy thrives on freedom of choice, tolerance and respect for divergent political interests, urging those behind the removal of the billboard to appreciate the fundamental principles of democratic participation.

“Democracy is about the people and their freedom to make choices. A citizen’s decision to support candidates across political party lines does not necessarily amount to a formal political coalition.

“While we recognise the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, we expect such regulations to be applied fairly, transparently and without political discrimination.”

The organisation also called on the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services (DSS) to closely monitor developments capable of overheating the polity and undermining peaceful political participation in Abia State.

“We urge the Police and the DSS to pay careful attention to actions and utterances capable of creating unnecessary political tension in the state.

“We equally urge members of Reality Organisation to remain peaceful, disciplined and resolute in their lawful grassroots engagements without allowing themselves to be provoked by the actions of others.

“Ultimately, elections are determined by the electorate, not by billboards or their removal. The democratic right of the people to freely choose their representatives must remain paramount,” the statement concluded.

The post Billboard controversy: Senator Orji Kalu’s politics anchored in the people, not Billboards — Reality organisation appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Two lovers arraigned over alleged N178.2m theft in Lagos
articles.summary:
Two lovers, Chukwu Amaka Goodness and Ajijie Ferdinand Eri, were on Tuesday arraigned before Justice D.I. Dipeolu of the Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos for an alleged N178.2m theft.

The Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) arraigned the duo.

The defendants are facing trial on a 13-count second amended charge bordering on stealing, conspiracy, fraudulent conversion and money laundering to the tune of N178,271,321.70.

Chukwu was a former employee of Nibel Enterprises owned by Bonnibel Ugochi, the petitioner.

One of the counts reads: “That you, Chukwu Amaka Goodness and Ajijie Ferdinand Eri, sometime in March 2025, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, conspired amongst yourselves to commit an offence to wit: retention of the total sum of N75,000,000.00 (Seventy-Five Million Naira) in an account nominated by you with account name ‘Ajijie Ferdinand’ and account number 6013401684, domiciled in Moniepoint Microfinance Bank, which sum you reasonably ought to have known forms part of the proceeds of your unlawful act, to wit: stealing, and you thereby committed an offence contrary to and punishable under Section 21(a) of the Money Laundering (Prohibition and Prevention) Act, 2022.”

Another count reads:”That you, CHUKWU AMAKA GOODNESS and AJIJIE FERDINAND ERI, sometime in March 2025, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, conspired amongst yourselves to commit an offence to wit: retention of the total sum of N38,364,921.70 (Thirty-Eight Million, Three Hundred and Sixty Four Thousand, Nine Hundred and Twenty One Naira, Seventy Kobo) in an account nominated by you with account name ‘Ferdinand Ajijie’ and account number 2729506481, domiciled in Zenith Bank Plc., which sum you reasonably ought to have known forms part of the proceeds of your unlawful act, to wit: stealing and you thereby committed an offence contrary to and punishable under Section 21(a) of the Money Laundering (Prohibition and Prevention Act), 2022.”

The defendants pleaded “guilty” to the charges when they were read to them in court.

Justice Dipeolu, thereafter, asked the defendants whether they pleaded guilty due to unfavourable conditions at the Correctional Centre or had been compelled to do so.

The defendants, however, denied being forced to enter the pleas, insisting that they voluntarily admitted committing the offences contained in the charges.

The prosecution counsel, Suleiman I. Suleiman, thereafter, urged the court to proceed with the review of facts in the case and called Ismail Saifullahi, an investigator with the EFCC, to testify.

Saifullahi, who was the sole witness, told the court that the defendants were arrested at the Force Criminal Investigation Department, Alagbon, Lagos, following their release from the police custody.

He also told the court that investigations traced the alleged diversion of proceeds from supermarket sales to accounts operated by the defendants.

According to him, Chukwu, who worked as a salesperson for the petitioner, Ugochi, connived with her boyfriend, Ajijie, to open a Moniepoint business account using his details, through which proceeds from the sales of goods at Nibel Enterprises were diverted.

“Goodness and Eri also received customers’ payments into their personal bank accounts and a Moniepoint account originally opened in the name of Eri and subsequently upgraded to a business account with the business name “Mibel Enterprises” mimicking “Nibel Enterprises” the business name of the petitioner, Bonnibel, while funds diverted from the sales of products and the stealing of goods belonging to the supermarket were traced to several bank accounts belonging to the defendants.”

Saifullahi also informed the court that a Camry car belonging to Ajijie, which is suspected to be proceeds of crime, was seized during investigation.

Consequently, Suleiman urged the court to convict the defendants and order the restitution of the sum of N79,835,950 to the petitioner, Ugochi.

During the proceedings, Justice Dipeolu reduced the charges from 13 to 12, noting that counts one and two were similar.

The judge held that “ Counts 1 and 2 are similar. Therefore, the counts are reduced from 13 to 12-count charge.”

The judge adjourned till December 1, 2026 for “ conviction and sentencing.”

The post Two lovers arraigned over alleged N178.2m theft in Lagos appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: NANS Lagos demands action against alleged fake, expired products
articles.summary:
The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Joint Campus Council, Lagos State Axis, has issued a seven-working-day ultimatum to the Federal Government and the Lagos State Government to take decisive action against the alleged production, distribution and repackaging of counterfeit and expired products at the Trade Fair Complex and other locations across Lagos State.

Speaking at a World Press Conference, the Chairman of NANS JCC Lagos State Axis, Comrade Quadri Ishola Odewunmi, described the situation as a public health emergency and an alleged attempt at mass murder, warning that the circulation of fake medicines, adulterated beverages and other unsafe consumables poses a serious threat to the lives of unsuspecting Nigerians, particularly students and vulnerable members of society.

 

Odewunmi expressed concern over the continued activities of suspected counterfeit product operators within the Trade Fair Complex despite previous enforcement operations by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).

He questioned the sustainability of existing enforcement efforts and called for stronger political will from both levels of government to bring the situation under control.

He further highlighted the potential health implications of consuming substandard and falsified medicines and contaminated products, noting that Nigerians should not have to fear that medications purchased to treat common illnesses could expose them to further health complications.

As part of its demands, NANS called for the immediate lawful sealing of the entire Trade Fair Complex, the establishment of a multi-agency Joint Task Force comprising NAFDAC, NDLEA, the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, as well as a comprehensive screening of every shop, warehouse, production facility and storage space within the complex.

The association also demanded the investigation and prosecution of all individuals found culpable, including the consideration of appropriate charges relating to deliberate endangerment of human lives where supported by evidence and applicable law.

It further insisted that the complex should only be reopened after a thorough screening exercise and the implementation of effective monitoring mechanisms.

Issuing a firm warning, the NANS chairman declared that should the two levels of government fail to demonstrate concrete action within seven working days, the association would consider relocating its Lagos State Secretariat to the Trade Fair Complex and mobilising students across Lagos and neighbouring states for a peaceful and sustained protest and occupation to demand accountability.

The association also condemned reported attacks on NAFDAC officials during enforcement operations, warning that Nigerian students would not be intimidated by threats or acts of violence.

It, however, emphasised that its proposed intervention would remain peaceful and directed against criminal activities rather than legitimate traders and business operators.

Reaffirming its position, NANS called on the Federal and Lagos State Governments to prioritise public health and human lives over commercial interests, insisting that the protection of consumers and the eradication of counterfeit and expired products must become an urgent government priority.

The association concluded with a strong declaration that the lives of ordinary Nigerians must not be sacrificed to commercial greed, demanding safe markets, effective regulation and accountability for all those involved in the production and circulation of dangerous products.

articles.title: Atiku: We won’t leave any part of Kogi behind
articles.summary:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has said that every part of Kogi State will feel the impact of his administration if he is elected president in 2027.

Atiku, according to a statement by the ADC Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, said this while speaking at a campaign rally in Lokoja, the Kogi State capital.

The ADC candidate promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill in Kogi Central, develop the Idah River Port and improve roads and water supply across Kogi East, and complete the Kabba to Egbe road in Kogi West. He noted that the promises were geared towards making life more affordable for citizens.

According to him, “To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers.

“To the people of Kogi Central, Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry.

“To the people of Kogi West, the Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route.”

The former Vice President, who stated that the strength of Kogi State lay in its people, also promised to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and to restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria to ease transport and production costs.

“Kogi’s strength lies in its people. I have seen your welcome today, and I will remember it. You deserve a government that turns your state’s potential into jobs, working infrastructure and a life your families can afford,” he stated.

 

The post Atiku: We won’t leave any part of Kogi behind appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Imo Airport reopens tomorrow as Uzodimma extends runway
articles.summary:
‎After an upgrade of some of its facilities, including the extension of the runway, Sam Mbakwe International Airport will reopen tomorrow.

The Airport was temporarily shut down for infrastructural intervention aimed at restoring the structural integrity of the existing runway, extending its operational length and strengthening associated aircraft movement infrastructure.

‎Imo State Commissioner for Information, Public Orientation and Strategy, Hon Declan Emelumba announced the news of the reopening of the airport.

‎He disclosed that the Imo State government bore the entire cost of the infrastructural upgrade at the Sam Mbakwe International Airport.

‎He said the rehabilitation became necessary following the deterioration of sections of the existing 2.7 kilometres runway.

According to the commissioner, the runway has now been extended to 3.2 kilometres with ashphalt resurfacing and strengthening of the existing taxiways.

‎”The rehabilitation and expansion of the Sam Mbakwe International Airport represent a significant infrastructural investment by His Excellency, Governor Hope Uzodimma,” he declared.

‎Emelumba further explained that the governor undertook the project to enhance the smooth movement of aircrafts especially during this Christmas period, that Imo people and others would be home.

‎According to him, Uzodimma anticipated increased traffic at the airport and decided to ensure that the facilities were upgraded.

‎He said the upgrade of the airport was part of a broader policy initiative of the government to make it easier for would be investors to access the state through the air.

articles.summary:
Germany's left-wing Die Linke party expels pro-Palestine lawmaker

Germany's far-left Die Linke party on Tuesday expelled local pro-Palestine lawmaker Vanessa Emde over her criticism of Israel.

Die Linke, which came first in local elections in Berlin in September, has been trying to hammer out a coalition deal with the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens.

Emde was newly elected as a local representative from the Neukolln district, which has a large Arab population.

Emde's expulsion on Tuesday - which was backed by more than two-thirds of Die Linke's lawmakers in the Berlin parliament - clears one potential hurdle to sealing a coalition deal with the SPD and the Greens.

Member of Germany's far-left Die Linke party Vanessa Emde addresses protesters in Berlin on 31 October 2026 (AFP)

Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), has strongly condemned the “treacherous attack” launched by the Iran-aligned Houthis on a tower in Saudi capital Riyadh’s financial centre.

The attack injured 11 people - two Saudi citizens and nine foreign nationals.

“This attack is a heinous crime and an aggression that reveals the danger of this militia’s terrorist approach and its disregard for innocent lives, which requires a decisive international stance to hold this militia accountable,” Albudaiwi said in a statement.

He added that the GCC member states stand with Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Houthis won't seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say
articles.summary:
Houthis won't seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have pushed as close as 60km to Aden, the temporary capital of the country's internationally recognised government, but they will not capture the city, Yemen's military said on Tuesday. 

"I'll speak to you frankly. The situation is not where we want it to be. But it's not as dire as reported," Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, told a group of reporters via video link.

Since fighting resumed in Yemen in July in parallel with the wider Iran war, the Houthis have rapidly advanced in Yemen, seizing territory from the internationally recognised government and its allies, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.

The Saudis have carried out air strikes on Yemen in support of their allies on the ground, while the Houthis have struck Saudi oil targets, airports and office towers.

Aden, now the target of Houthi missile and drone strikes, had previously not seen major hostilities since street battles in 2015, soon after the internationally recognised government fled Houthi-run Sanaa and made the port city its base.

Reporting by Reuters

The building in Saudi capital houses the offices of the country's sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund

Riyadh's skyline, featuring the PIF tower, on 22 November 2026 (AFP)

A building housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund in Riyadh has been hit for the second time in under a week.

Riyadh called Tuesday's suspected drone attack by Yemen's Houthi-aligned forces a "cowardly terrorist attack".

Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence reported that 11 people were injured in the strike and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The PIF Tower was previously hit in an attack last Thursday.

It is one of the Saudi capital's tallest buildings and is part of the King Abdullah Financial District.

Yemen's Houthis have demonstrated an ability to consistently strike prominent targets within Saudi Arabia, even as Riyadh launches its own air strikes on Yemen.

Earlier in November, a building belonging to the kingdom's oil giant Aramco was damaged in an attack in Riyadh.

In October, an attack on Riyadh's airport killed at least 14 people.

Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund skyscraper

Read More »

Tuesday's attack in Riyadh came as Saudi warplanes struck buses and trucks in Wadi Maabaq in Yemen’s Lahij governorate, killing as many as 25 people and wounding six, the Saba news agency reports.

Residents told Saba that badly burnt human remains were still inside one of two buses hit in the attack, hampering identification.

They said Saudi warplanes continued circling overhead, blocking ambulance crews and residents from reaching those caught in the strikes and worsening the toll.

Saudi Arabia resumed fighting in Yemen in July after years of an uneasy ceasefire. Since then Houthi forces have made significant gains, reaching Yemen's southern coastline and securing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab waterway, which connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea.

Control of the waterway means that Yemen's Houthi-led Sanaa government controls shipping traffic going up to the Suez Canal in Egypt.

Yemen's war, which started with a Houthi offensive in 2014, has claimed the lives of close to 400,000 people, according to some estimates.

A large number of Yemeni civilians have died due to Saudi-led coalition bombardment and an economic siege imposed by Riyadh on Houthi-held territory.

articles.title: Amnesty calls on UK to stop Israeli organisation promoting West Bank settlements
articles.summary:
Amnesty calls on UK to stop Israeli organisation promoting West Bank settlements

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Tue, 11/24/2026 - 15:13

Shivat Zion, whose website encourages moving to illegal settlements from abroad, is currently touring the UK

Cattle gather in an enclosure at a farm run by Israeli settlers near the Palestinian town of Duma in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on 13 October 2026 (AFP)

Off

Amnesty International UK is calling on the British government to bar Shivat Zion, an Israeli non-profit organisation dedicated to promoting Jewish immigration to Israel, from encouraging UK citizens to relocate to the occupied West Bank.

The call came ahead of a scheduled UK tour by Shivat Zion, which started on Sunday in Glasgow and is set to include events in Gateshead, Leeds, Manchester, Birmingham, London, Bournemouth and Brighton. 

A spokesperson for the group told Jewish News earlier this month: "Making Aliyah is a major life decision, and having the opportunity to speak face to face with professionals, ask questions and get reliable answers can make all the difference." 

Aliyah is a Hebrew word that translates as "elevation" or "going up", and is primarily used to refer to Jews from outside Israel moving to Israel.

Kristyan Benedict, a campaign manager at Amnesty, said the British government's recognition of Israel’s “unlawful occupation and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians… must now become meaningful action to meet the UK's obligations under international law”.

He clarified that this "must include preventing any activity on UK soil that contributes to Israel's system of apartheid or its unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory.”

"The UK’s new approach to Israel must mean investigating and acting against those enabling illegal occupation, ethnic cleansing, and apartheid. You can’t condemn occupation while waving its promoters through,” Benedict said.

Promoting a life in illegal settlements

Middle East Eye previously reported that multiple pages on Shivat Zion's website promote illegal settlements in the West Bank, including a kibbutz in Gush Etzion.

Israeli non-profit helping Britons move to occupied West Bank to tour UK cities

Read More »

The site also features a page giving "an overview of the process required to convert a foreign teacher's license in Israel", and advertises teacher training in Gush Etzion.

A private section of the website, accessed by Jewish Anti-Zionist Action (Jaza), a British campaign group, and seen by MEE, allows potential emigrants to calculate the cost of moving to different locations.

These include the illegal West Bank settlements of Efrat, Maale Adumim and Karnei Shomron, as well as Katzrin in the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights in Syria. 

MEE revealed last month that Israeli government agencies held a recruitment drive in London encouraging British doctors to emigrate amid an exodus of medical professionals from the country.

A Jaza activist who gained entry to the event reported that attendees were handed leaflets from medical providers and health funds - such as Terem and Clalit - which run centres in illegal Israeli settlements across the occupied West Bank. 

Shivast Zion was filmed in a report for Declassified UK offering to help British citizens move to an illegal settlement in the West Bank, with an "encouragement officer" saying on a Zoom call: “You’re next to the Arabs; you’ll hear their mosques but apart from that it’s a great living standard.”

articles.title: Saudi finance minister claims kingdom can withstand prolonged Houthi conflict
articles.summary:
Saudi finance minister claims kingdom can withstand prolonged Houthi conflict

Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan says the kingdom is “resilient enough to withstand a prolonged conflict” with Yemen’s Houthis.

Speaking to reporters, al-Jadaan dismissed as “a total mistake” any expectation that attacks on civilian infrastructure or “blackmail by missiles” would force Riyadh to compromise its national security.

He said Saudi Arabia plans to reduce its budget deficit to 3.6 percent of GDP in 2027, compared with an estimated 4.9 percent this year, despite the escalating fighting.

The Iran-backed Houthis say their missile and drone campaign aims to force Riyadh to withdraw support for Yemen’s government.

Al-Jadaan said reduced oil production had driven a 2.1 percent contraction in Saudi GDP this year.

articles.title: 'Political theatre': Campaigners hit out at EU hypocrisy as Cop31 ends in chaos
articles.summary:
'Political theatre': Campaigners hit out at EU hypocrisy as Cop31 ends in chaos

Submitted by
Katherine Hearst
on
Tue, 11/24/2026 - 13:44

Developing countries say they felt kept in the dark and were not consulted during the drafting of the final text

Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of Cop31 Negotiations Chris Bowen at a plenary session at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, 22 November 2026 (Reuters)

Off

On Sunday, fraught global climate talks in Turkey, the longest ever in the climate conference’s history, ground to a halt, with no deal. The EU, UK and allies rejected the draft text over its failure to mention fossil fuels.

At the closing plenary, Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien, on behalf of the EU, rejected the text, saying it “does not respond to the science, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required… that does not even mention fossil fuels”.

His words were met with applause. But they rang hollow for developing countries, many of whom also rejected the text over its weak language on climate finance.

After delivering his intervention, O’Brien and EU Climate Minister Wopke Hoekstra walked out of the plenary to hold a press huddle while developing nations were speaking about the need for climate finance.

While the EU, UK and allies cited the omission of fossil fuels from the text as their main reason for rejecting it, climate justice campaigners reported that developed countries and EU officials had spent the duration of the talks blocking measures which would require them to make fresh finance commitments.

“The EU used fossil fuels as the main reason for their rejection of the text. But the other issue, or what I would call the most important issue, is climate finance,” Harjeet Singh, strategic adviser to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative and the global convenor of the Fill the Fund campaign, told Middle East Eye.

“If you listened to what other countries said, like Panama, Ghana, the Marshall Islands, their reasons were no money for adaptation, no money for loss and damage.”

Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, developed countries are required to provide finance to help developing countries cut emissions and adapt to climate impacts.

According to the UN’s latest report, published earlier this month, developing countries will need about $300bn annually in adaptation funding by 2035. 

At Cop26 in 2021, developed countries agreed to at least double adaptation finance by 2025, with 2019 levels, $19bn, as a benchmark.

Last year, they agreed to a call to “at least triple” adaptation finance by 2035. But the final text left ambiguities around the baseline year.

An earlier draft of this year’s text, released on 16 November, stipulated a target annual figure of at least $120bn, with a baseline of $40bn a year.

But the sums were quietly dropped from subsequent drafts. Climate justice campaigners laid the blame for this squarely at the doors of the EU and wealthier countries who they say "came with nothing" and thwarted progress on discussions around climate finance.

During this year’s “Contributor Dialogue” at the conference, which aimed to fill the starved fund, a handful of developed countries pledged just $30m, significantly down from last year’s sum of $120m.

“So we have a fund that no one wants to fill,” Singh said.

Dead in the water

Even before the summit had started, Hoekstra set the tone for negotiations by proclaiming climate finance “dead in the water”.

“They entered negotiations with that bad faith and blocked every single track which is important for developing countries,” Singh told MEE.

According to Climate Action Network, the EU and other developed countries refused to engage on a baseline for tripling adaptation finance.

Cop31 draft agreement ‘the worst ever', campaigners warn

Read More »

“We agreed on the baseline, I was witness to that process in 2019,” Singh said.

“So they just want to create new processes and new loops so that we can just continue talking.”

Singh also pointed to what he described as the hypocrisy of the EU and wealthy countries’ stance on fossil fuel language in the draft text.

"Norway and Ireland, who were arguing for the inclusion of fossil fuel language in the text, are back home expanding fossil fuel production,” he said.

The EU’s own “roadmaps” for transitions away from fossil fuels have drawn criticism for restating existing policies that are not aligned with the 1.5 degree temperature goal.

Brandon Wu, director of policy and campaigns at Action Aid USA, slammed the EU’s transition plans as a “smokescreen”.

“They’re using the rhetoric around fossil fuels to make themselves look like champions," Wu told reporters.

For Singh, a Cop veteran who has attended the last 18 conferences, the EU’s actions are tantamount to little more than “political theatre”.

“Do your work. We need to move beyond these theatrics and take real action, rather than simply claiming leadership. Be a real leader. Provide the money. Take action at home in line with your fair share of the global effort,” he said.

‘Extremely disrespected’

Campaigners told Middle East Eye that the talks’ meltdown was also due in part to the weak and untransparent facilitation by the joint presidents, Australia and Turkey.

“There was no stocktaking plenary where countries could share their opinion, where things could be dragged out in the open. When they said they would publish text, they didn’t do so,” Andreas Sieber, associate director of global policy at 350.org, told MEE.

'Norway and Ireland, who were arguing for the inclusion of fossil fuel language in the text, are back home expanding fossil fuel production'

- Harjeet Singh, strategic adviser to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative

MEE understands that many developing countries felt they were left in the dark and not consulted while the text was being drafted. 

Cop presidents usually release printed versions of drafts for parties to review. But this year, only selected groups were shown excerpts, leaving many developing countries feeling “extremely disrespected and extremely badly treated,” one observer said.

Hanen Keskes of Greenpeace Mena said that the process of revising the second draft of the Cop text was very unclear.

“From what I've heard from parties, they had not been consulted,” Keskes told MEE. “It was very unclear what progress happened between the 19th and 22nd on other agenda items that were quite important.

“When the new text came out on Saturday night, it was essentially the same text from the 19th. So clearly no consultation had been done.”

The acrimony was summed up in a searing rebuke of the Cop presidency by Ghana’s Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, who was “rudely cut off” during her delivery by Murat Kurum, Cop31 president and Turkey's environment minister.

“This, excellency, is an example of the levels of disrespect we have endured and continue to express our objection to. It absolutely does not respect multilateralism,” she said.
